# RFC-0004: Measurement And Toolchain Contract

> **Version:** 0.32.0 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** impl
> **Owners:** @Zihua Wu

**References:** [RFC-0009](../rfc/RFC-0009.md)

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0004:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0004c-summary"></a>

This RFC governs measurements and the toolchains that execute them: Eval and Bench semantics and result normalization, the InferLab-owned release-versioned measurement toolchains, and workload-attached Nsight Systems profiling. Servers, server cases, server records, and readiness semantics are defined by [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md); records by [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md). [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md) holds the specification overview and the authority map.

*Since: v0.1.0*

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS] Eval And Bench Measurements (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-measurements"></a>

InferLab MUST support reusable workspace-local Eval and serving-Bench definitions.

A static serving-Bench definition MAY omit its definition `kind`; omission MUST resolve to `serving`. An explicit definition `kind` MUST remain `serving` or `adaptive-serving`. The effective definition kind MUST be preserved in canonical merged workspace output, dry-run, execution, and record evidence whether it was declared or defaulted.

An Eval definition MUST be able to express the evaluated task or dataset selection, bounded sample policy, positive fixed repeated-trial count, primary metric, pass threshold, and timeout when those values apply.

A serving-Bench definition MUST be able to express prompt-source parameters, prompt representation, input and output shape, concurrency-limited load, request-rate-limited load, arrival burstiness, request-count or duration policy, cache start policy, optional server-metric collection, artifact level governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-ARTIFACT-LEVEL](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-artifact-level), timeout, and the request-body fragment governed by [RFC-0004:C-INFERENCE-REQUESTS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-inference-requests) when those values apply.

A concurrency serving-Bench definition MAY declare the non-negative integer field `warmup_prompts_per_concurrency`. Omission MUST resolve to zero. The field applies to every request source governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-request-sources), where one materialized population entry produces one request.

For each expanded concurrency case with concurrency `c`, InferLab MUST resolve the warmup request count as `c * warmup_prompts_per_concurrency`. A value that cannot be represented by the supported request-count domain MUST fail definition resolution.

A zero resolved warmup request count MUST preserve the existing single profiling-phase behavior.

A positive resolved warmup request count MUST lower to an AIPerf-native warmup phase before the case profiling phase. The warmup phase MUST retain the case concurrency, effective request-source policy, selected route, served model, and effective request-body fragment. AIPerf MAY add its native phase marker to the effective warmup prompt or message; InferLab MUST preserve the phase-tagged native request artifact rather than claiming byte-identical profiling input.

The frozen request population MUST contain the resolved warmup request count plus the profiling request count, use sequential sampling through the one sampler shared by the native phases, and contain enough entries that neither phase wraps or reuses an entry. InferLab MUST preserve the native conversation identity and benchmark phase for emitted warmup and profiling request records.

Warmup requests MUST be excluded from normalized metrics and from the case completed and failed profiling-request counts. A positive warmup succeeds only when the native phase artifacts contain exactly the resolved number of warmup request records and every such record is terminal without an error or cancellation. A missing, incomplete, errored, or cancelled warmup request MUST fail the case. The failure MUST report the expected, observed-completed, errored, cancelled, and missing warmup counts and preserve the available process outcome and, at the `diagnostic` artifact level governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-ARTIFACT-LEVEL](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-artifact-level), the raw AIPerf phase artifacts.

The declared warmup multiplier and each concurrency case's resolved warmup request count MUST be preserved in dry-run and execution evidence.

A workload suite MUST be able to select an Eval gate and one or more Eval and Bench measurements; a recipe selects those measurements only through its named workload suite.

A Bench guarded by an Eval gate MUST be skipped when that gate does not succeed.

An OpenAI-compatible completions smoke definition MAY declare its prompt, maximum-token limit, and timeout independently of a server endpoint or execution engine. Omission MUST resolve the prompt to `Hello`, the maximum-token limit to `16`, and the timeout to `60` seconds. Explicit values MUST replace those defaults subject to the same validation. The effective prompt, maximum-token limit, and timeout MUST be preserved in canonical merged workspace output, dry-run, execution, and record evidence.

The Eval definition kind MUST determine the execution boundary without a separate user-selectable engine setting.

An OpenAI-compatible completions smoke measurement MUST NOT require or launch an installed measurement-toolchain runtime.

The smoke request MUST use the resolved public completions path and served model, the effective prompt and maximum-token limit, non-streaming generation, and zero temperature. It MUST NOT accept the Eval and Bench request-body fragment.

A successful smoke measurement MUST receive a 2xx HTTP response containing a JSON object with a non-empty `choices` array whose first element contains a string `text` value.

A transport error, timeout, interruption, non-2xx response, malformed JSON response, missing or empty `choices` array, or a missing or non-string first-choice `text` value MUST fail the smoke measurement.

Every smoke attempt MUST preserve the effective HTTP request, elapsed time and terminal outcome, plus failure evidence when the outcome is failure.

When the HTTP operation returns a complete response, smoke evidence MUST additionally preserve its status, body size, and raw body artifact.

When a valid `choices` array is parsed, smoke evidence MUST preserve its choice count.

lm-eval measurements MUST execute through the Eval runtime fixed by the invoking InferLab release.

Serving Bench measurements MUST execute through the AIPerf runtime fixed by the invoking InferLab release.

A serving-Bench definition MAY set `server_metrics = true`; omission MUST resolve to false. When false, InferLab MUST NOT ask AIPerf to scrape a server-metrics endpoint. When true, the resolved target server capability MUST supply one AIPerf-compatible server-metrics endpoint containing its logical path and public-or-named-port binding plus the exact control-plane-resolved URL. The measurement runtime MUST pass that exact frozen URL to AIPerf and MUST NOT reconstruct or alter it. InferLab MUST fail preflight before the first transport request when the capability is absent or invalid.

Server-metric collection MUST run through AIPerf's native `serverMetrics` configuration and MUST request JSON export. InferLab MUST NOT substitute framework logs, a framework-native benchmark client, or an independently timed scraper. The required native raw artifact is the case run directory's unchanged `server_metrics_export.json`. An AIPerf launch failure, a non-zero profile outcome not accepted by the complete all-inference-error rule in [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-SLO](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-slo), or a completed profile without that artifact MUST fail the case while preserving available process and raw evidence. When AIPerf returns zero and emits the required artifact, InferLab MUST accept the native AIPerf classification of recoverable scrape errors and MUST NOT parse log text, infer failure from metric gaps, or inspect private in-process state to impose a second collection-success policy.

For a successful `speed_bench` case with server metrics enabled, `profile_export_aiperf.json` and `server_metrics_export.json` MUST be inputs to the release-pinned AIPerf `speed-bench-report` CLI. The measurement runtime MUST invoke that CLI once with `--format csv --metric accept_length` and once with `--format csv --metric accept_rate`, using the one case run directory as input and distinct preserved CSV output paths.

Each report MUST contain exactly one row for the served model and one non-empty cell for the case's resolved SPEED-Bench category. InferLab MUST expose the decimal cell from the acceptance-length report as the scalar `acceptance_length` and the decimal cell from the acceptance-rate report as the scalar `acceptance_rate`. These normalized values inherit the release-pinned AIPerf report's aggregation and decimal-rounding semantics; InferLab MUST NOT recompute them from server-metric series, transport-token counts, or framework logs.

A missing or duplicate model row, missing category column, empty or non-numeric cell, non-finite value, acceptance length below one, acceptance rate outside the inclusive range from zero through one, or non-zero report-process outcome MUST fail successful-result normalization and identify the report and cell. A non-SPEED-Bench source MUST omit `acceptance_length` and `acceptance_rate` even when raw server metrics are collected.

Evidence MUST preserve both report invocations, process outcomes, CSV artifacts, and the two unchanged native JSON inputs. InferLab MUST NOT maintain a second server-metric-name matcher or claim a framework metric identity that the AIPerf report does not expose.

A measurement client result MUST carry result envelope version `1`.

The measurement runtime MUST reject an Eval or Bench result whose envelope version it does not support, failing that case with an error naming the unsupported version.

Static concurrency and request-rate definitions MUST expand into deterministic ordered cases before execution.

Adaptive-serving definition, SLO evaluation, request-count success semantics, and rate search MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-SLO](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-slo).

Manual and closed-loop execution under the same invoking InferLab release and toolchain identity MUST use the same case planning, cache preparation, timeout, AIPerf version, result normalization, and evidence semantics for the same effective Bench definition and serving snapshot.

Each Bench case MUST report profiling-phase `completed_requests` and `failed_requests` as integer counts derived only from native records tagged for the profiling phase.

Bench normalization schema `aiperf-summary-v1` MUST map AIPerf `request_throughput.avg`, `output_token_throughput.avg`, and `total_token_throughput.avg` to the scalar InferLab metrics `request_throughput`, `output_throughput`, and `total_token_throughput`, respectively.

The schema MUST expose backend-observed prompt-token count, request latency, and TTFT as the stable distribution families `prompt_tokens`, `request_latency_ms`, and `ttft_ms`. With AIPerf server token counting enabled, `prompt_tokens` MUST retain the backend-reported final input-token count after the locally frozen or server-owned rendering selected by the resolved prompt kind; it MUST NOT use a source-content estimate.

For a Bench whose request source fixes every effective output-token limit at one, TPOT is not applicable and the normalized result MUST omit the `tpot_ms` family.

For a Bench whose request source guarantees every effective output-token limit is at least two, the schema MUST expose TPOT as the stable distribution family `tpot_ms`.

For each applicable distribution family, the schema MUST map AIPerf statistics `avg`, `min`, `max`, `std`, `p50`, `p90`, `p95`, and `p99` to InferLab metric-name prefixes `mean`, `min`, `max`, `stddev`, `p50`, `p90`, `p95`, and `p99`, respectively.

Each normalized distribution key MUST be composed as `<prefix>_<family>`. The prompt-token keys MUST be `mean_prompt_tokens`, `min_prompt_tokens`, `max_prompt_tokens`, `stddev_prompt_tokens`, `p50_prompt_tokens`, `p90_prompt_tokens`, `p95_prompt_tokens`, and `p99_prompt_tokens`. The request-latency keys MUST be `mean_request_latency_ms`, `min_request_latency_ms`, `max_request_latency_ms`, `stddev_request_latency_ms`, `p50_request_latency_ms`, `p90_request_latency_ms`, `p95_request_latency_ms`, and `p99_request_latency_ms`. The TTFT keys MUST be `mean_ttft_ms`, `min_ttft_ms`, `max_ttft_ms`, `stddev_ttft_ms`, `p50_ttft_ms`, `p90_ttft_ms`, `p95_ttft_ms`, and `p99_ttft_ms`. When applicable, the TPOT keys MUST be `mean_tpot_ms`, `min_tpot_ms`, `max_tpot_ms`, `stddev_tpot_ms`, `p50_tpot_ms`, `p90_tpot_ms`, `p95_tpot_ms`, and `p99_tpot_ms`.

The schema MUST source the prompt-token family from AIPerf `input_sequence_length`, the request-latency family from `request_latency`, the TTFT family from `time_to_first_token`, and the TPOT family from `inter_token_latency`.

InferLab MUST treat AIPerf `inter_token_latency` as a private source name for AIPerf's per-request `(request latency - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1)` value. The normalized result MUST NOT expose a duplicate ITL metric family for that same value.

When per-request cache-read observations are required by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state), the schema MUST expose `prompt_cache_read_ratio` from the summed per-request prompt-cache-read tokens divided by the summed per-request prompt tokens. When those observations are not required and AIPerf reports a finite `overall_usage_prompt_cache_read_pct.avg` profiling value in the inclusive range from zero through one hundred, the schema MUST expose `prompt_cache_read_ratio` as that value divided by one hundred. Both paths retain token-volume-weighted profiling-window semantics.

When per-request cache-read observations are not required and AIPerf does not report `overall_usage_prompt_cache_read_pct.avg`, the normalized result MUST omit `prompt_cache_read_ratio`. A reported non-numeric, non-finite, or out-of-range aggregate value MUST fail successful-result normalization.

The normalization schema MUST preserve AIPerf's profiling request window, token accounting, and percentile semantics for those source fields.

A successful Bench case with at least one completed profiling request MUST fail validation when a required throughput scalar, prompt-token statistic, request-latency statistic, or TTFT statistic is absent, non-numeric, or non-finite. A successful Bench with at least one completed profiling request whose request source makes TPOT applicable MUST also fail validation when a required TPOT statistic is absent, non-numeric, or non-finite.

A request-level SLO case with zero completed profiling requests MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-SLO](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-slo) and MUST NOT fabricate distribution metrics for an empty completed-request population.

A failed Bench case MUST finalize as one failed Bench-record case with explicit error text, stdout and stderr paths, available request counts, produced partial raw artifacts, and an empty or explicitly partial metric set.

A failed Bench case MUST preserve process outcome when a measurement process started.

Serving-Bench cache start, reset, conditioning, phase ordering, preparation failures, case-budget ownership, and cache-derived metric requirements MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state).

InferLab MUST record each Eval or Bench measurement's identity, effective parameters, effective invocation, structured metrics, produced raw result artifacts, failure, and skip reason when applicable.

**Rationale:** Eval and serving performance are stable InferLab measurement concepts even when serving frameworks change. The built-in smoke is an endpoint protocol check that needs no external evaluation engine, while lm-eval and AIPerf remain release-owned external engines for dataset evaluation and serving Bench. A native excluded warmup phase lets a declared workload exercise shape-dependent JIT, allocation, and connection setup without discarding measured requests or teaching the control plane to parse framework-specific logs. Keeping case, gate, cache preparation, warmup, adaptive, lifecycle, and evidence semantics in InferLab preserves one experiment workflow across those execution boundaries.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-INFERLAB-TOOLCHAIN] InferLab Measurement Toolchain (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-inferlab-toolchain"></a>

The public CLI MUST provide `inferlab toolchain install` to install the lm-eval and Bench runtimes fixed by the running InferLab release.

One explicit installation MUST provide independently isolated lm-eval and Bench dependency closures under one version-and-platform installation identity.

The installed Eval runtime MUST contain the release-pinned lm-eval engine and every InferLab-bundled Eval task closure fixed by that release.

The installed Bench runtime MUST contain the release-pinned AIPerf engine.

`toolchain install` and lm-eval or Bench preflight MUST support glibc Linux x86_64 and aarch64.

`toolchain install` and lm-eval or Bench preflight MUST fail with an explicit unsupported-platform error on other operating systems, C libraries, and architectures.

A workflow that selects neither lm-eval nor Bench MUST NOT require a supported measurement-toolchain platform or an installed measurement toolchain.

The toolchain MUST be installed directly at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/inferlab/toolchains/<inferlab-version>/<platform>/`, using the platform's conventional XDG data default when `XDG_DATA_HOME` is unset.

Installed prefixes MUST NOT be relocated after installation.

A complete matching installation MUST be identified by completion metadata that matches the invoking InferLab version, host platform, release manifest and lock digests, runner digests and versions, installed lm-eval and AIPerf versions, and the bundled Eval task-closure digest fixed by the release.

The bundled Eval task-closure digest MUST cover every bundled task definition, prompt asset, dataset asset, and scorer implementation consumed by lm-eval.

Installation MUST serialize concurrent writers.

Installation MUST consume the package definition fixed by the InferLab release without updating it.

Installation MUST verify both runtime closures and the bundled Eval task closure before publishing completion metadata.

A matching complete installation MUST make `toolchain install` an idempotent no-op.

An explicit `toolchain install` MUST either replace an incomplete or release-mismatched installation with a complete matching installation or fail without publishing matching completion metadata.

When replacing an installation fails because the installation path is held by live processes, the failure MUST identify the holding processes. Identification covers the holders visible to the invoking user; holders beyond that visibility can exist and the identified set is not exhaustive.

Dry-run and experiment execution MUST only validate the matching installed runtime required by selected lm-eval or Bench measurements.

Dry-run and experiment execution MUST NOT install, repair, update, or select a different toolchain version.

When a selected lm-eval or Bench measurement requires a missing or incomplete matching runtime, dry-run and execution MUST fail before the first experiment effect and identify `inferlab toolchain install` as the required action.

Different InferLab versions MUST be able to coexist. Automatic update, garbage collection, registry publication, and general-purpose toolchain management commands are outside this contract.

**Rationale:** Dataset evaluation and serving performance measurement use release-owned external engines rather than the model-serving dependency closure. One explicit versioned installation keeps workspaces small and serving locks stable, while isolated lm-eval and Bench closures prevent their unrelated dependencies and platform requirements from perturbing each other. Binding bundled Eval assets and scorer code to the same completion identity prevents two installations of one InferLab release from silently executing different tasks. The built-in OpenAI smoke remains available without this installation because it adds no external evaluation engine.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING] Workload-Attached Profiling (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-workload-profiling"></a>

InferLab supports two workload-attached capture mechanisms: `managed_collection`, in which InferLab wraps each target process with a managed Nsight Systems collection, and `engine_trace`, in which the serving framework's internal profiler writes per-rank trace artifacts under InferLab-directed storage. A server, its cases, and invocation-scoped overrides MAY declare `profiler.mechanism`; omission MUST resolve to `managed_collection` under [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution).

When profiling is enabled for a server, InferLab MUST prepare every launched process rank of each model-serving replica declared as profile-capable by the selected integration as a capture target of the effective mechanism for later Eval or Bench measurements.

A server, server case, or invocation-scoped server setting MAY request capture-target preparation.

Profiler declarations MUST NOT silently drop: when profiling resolves off for a server (no `profiling = true` and no requested capture), an effective declaration of `profiler.mechanism` or profiler escape inputs MUST fail resolution with a typed error naming the declaration and the enable-profiling remediation.

A server prepared with capture targets MUST NOT bound its readiness wait by the effective server readiness timeout ([RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution)): capture instrumentation multiplies startup cost by an unpredictable factor, and a budget chosen for uninstrumented startup converts progressing servers into false failures. The capture-armed readiness wait terminates only by readiness success, process-group exit, or operator interruption, each with deterministic evidence.

Each blocking process-status or endpoint attempt within capture-armed readiness MUST use the effective `readiness_attempt_timeout_seconds` governed by [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution). Attempt expiry MUST return to the unbounded readiness loop so it can retry and re-evaluate process exit or operator interruption.

An Eval or Bench execution MUST support an explicit profiling-capture request without changing the selected named measurement definition.

A usable capture target MUST identify the target, its logical role, replica, process, and rank boundary, its capture mechanism, its supported framework-neutral window-control kinds, its control mechanism, its profiler storage, and its report finalization or retrieval strategy.

The selected framework integration MUST declare which capture mechanisms it supports and the framework-specific profiler controls and launch inputs each supported mechanism needs. The integration MUST reject a requested mechanism it does not support before launch.

InferLab MUST retain authority for profiler process lifecycle, capture planning, window control, collection finalization, report verification, cleanup, and authoritative evidence.

Preparing profiler output and arming managed collection across every selected target MUST consume one effective `capture_arm_deadline_seconds` budget. That budget MUST begin immediately before the first profiler-output preparation or collection-arm external action. A later target or command MUST consume the remaining arm budget and MUST NOT restart it. Failure to prepare output or arm any selected target, including expiry of that budget, MUST fail the containing profiled measurement before measured client work begins.

For an engine-trace capture target, InferLab MUST assign a persistent trace directory under record-owned runtime storage, keyed by server definition and replica, and supply it to the integration at render time, and the integration MUST render that directory into the target's framework-native launch configuration so engine processes write trace artifacts into it directly. Trace artifacts are measurement evidence: they MUST NOT be directed to machine-local scratch or cache storage, and InferLab MUST NOT recopy them into the record after the fact.

An engine-trace capture target MUST be rejected when the selected placement is not entirely local to the controlling machine or when the launch is image-backed: InferLab defines no remote or in-container trace retrieval.

For an engine-trace target, artifact flush completion is judged by coverage verification alone, never by the window-closing control response, whose latency carries no completion information. Coverage verification MUST confirm that the storage delta since collection arming contains at least one new trace artifact per device of the target replica's whole-replica device count, counted without framework-specific file naming. Engine-internal profilers write one artifact per engine worker process, which the device count bounds, while the control-plane rank model counts entry processes. The trace directory is dedicated to the target replica, so unrelated writes cannot fabricate coverage. A delta smaller than the device count MUST be treated as capture failure. Engine-trace targets declare no profiler escape inputs in this version.

For the managed-collection mechanism, a server MAY declare profiler escape inputs, and each of its model-serving roles MAY declare escape inputs that merge into the server's: scalar escapes replace, launch and start option lists concatenate with the role's options after the server's, the trace set replaces, and environment entries merge per key with the role value winning.

Managed-collection escape option lists are declared separately for the profiler launch command and the collection-start command, and InferLab MUST splice each list ahead of its managed argv tail so that a managed value wins on collision.

The managed-collection profiler executable, trace set, sampling, and context-switch escapes are dedicated fields: the trace set replaces the managed default trace set, sampling and context switch each replace their managed default, and the free-list option form of a dedicated field MUST be rejected toward the dedicated field.

A managed-collection escape environment map MUST apply to every InferLab-managed Nsight Systems command for the target, including profiler launch, collection start, session inspection, and collection stop. Entries on the profiler launch command MUST reach the wrapped server process through launch-command inheritance. For collection-start, session-inspection, and collection-stop commands, InferLab MUST apply that environment only to the command process and MUST NOT separately propagate it to or modify the wrapped server process. Environment keys MUST be POSIX identifiers, rejected at workspace load naming the escape field and the key; the rendered environment prefix terminates option parsing with a separator before the first assignment, so no key can be parsed as an option of the environment utility.

A managed-collection escape option that names a managed profiler fact — session identity; report storage, export, and overwrite lifecycle; capture-range mechanics; or launch wait behavior — MUST be rejected when the workspace is loaded, naming the escape field and the offending option, in long, short, attached short-option-value, and abbreviated long forms — any strict prefix of a managed long option name, which either resolves to the managed option or is an ambiguity. A standalone `-` or `--` token in an escape option list MUST likewise be rejected at workspace load, because it ends option parsing and displaces the managed argv tail into positionals of the wrapped command.

The record MUST preserve the effective mechanism of every capture target, both the raw escape declaration and the effective profiler invocations it produced when escapes apply, and the assigned trace storage of engine-trace targets.

Profiling an Eval or Bench MUST remain an observation mode attached to that measurement and MUST NOT create a separate workload kind.

A profiling request MUST bind to a managed server record and resolve every prepared process-rank target before measured client work starts.

Each capture window MUST have a semantic identity and a binding to the measured Eval phase or Bench case before the window opens.

A static capture plan for a range-backed target MUST enumerate every expected capture window and compute the expected range count for each selected target before collection is armed.

A static capture plan MUST preserve the mapping from each framework range index to its semantic capture-window identity.

A profiling request that uses a range-backed target MUST fail before measured client work when its capture windows cannot be enumerated in advance.

A dynamic measurement MAY use an external-session control kind instead when every selected target advertises that control kind.

InferLab MUST open a capture window before its bound measured phase begins.

InferLab MUST close the capture window after the measured phase completes or fails.

InferLab MUST attempt to close an opened capture window when measured client work fails.

Each framework window-control action MUST establish its effective `capture_control_deadline_seconds` budget immediately before dispatching the control request. That budget MUST cover the complete HTTP request, including connection establishment and response consumption. The action MUST NOT impose a shorter fixed connection or response cap. Expiry of a window-opening action budget MUST fail the containing profiled measurement. For a managed-collection target, expiry of a window-closing action budget MUST be treated as a window-closing control failure and adjudicated by coverage verification below. For an engine-trace target, window closing is a dispatch into the finalization phase: InferLab MUST dispatch the close request when the measured phase ends, and the dispatch, response consumption, flush waiting, and coverage verification MUST consume the one global finalization budget below rather than a window-control action budget. A delivery failure of an engine-trace close — connection refusal, a dead engine process, or a prompt error status — MUST be treated as a window-closing control failure and adjudicated by coverage verification; a slow or absent response MUST be preserved as neutral flush-pending evidence and MUST NOT by itself fail the capture.

For asynchronous report generation, InferLab MUST finalize managed profiler collection before verifying report coverage or performing destructive server cleanup.

Collection-state inspection, any required collection stop, engine-trace window-close dispatch and response consumption, asynchronous report completion, engine-trace flush completion, and coverage verification across all selected targets MUST consume one effective `capture_finalization_deadline_seconds` budget. That budget MUST begin when the measurement business result becomes terminal, before the first finalization action. A fallback action or later target MUST consume that budget’s remaining time and MUST NOT restart the configured duration. Expiry of the finalization budget MUST fail the containing profiled measurement while preserving the terminal measurement business result.

After collection finalization, InferLab MUST verify coverage for every planned range on every required range-backed target and every required rank trace artifact on every required engine-trace target.

A required report reference or rank trace artifact missing after collection finalization MUST be treated as capture failure.

A measurement requiring profiling MUST fail when target resolution, window-opening control, measured client work, collection finalization, required report generation, or required coverage verification fails.

A window-closing control failure MUST be preserved as evidence and adjudicated by coverage verification: the capture succeeds despite it when every required report and rank trace artifact verifies, and fails carrying both the coverage and control evidence when one does not.

Measurement evidence MUST preserve the capture plan, window identities, selected role, replica, process, and rank targets, capture mechanism per target, range mapping, control actions, collection finalization, report and trace-artifact references, verification outcomes, and failure evidence when those facts apply.

**Rationale:** Profiling observes ordinary correctness and performance work. Two mechanisms share one window, budget, and evidence spine because the operator question — what happened inside this measured phase — is mechanism-neutral, while the artifact producers differ: managed collection owns its report lifecycle outright, whereas an engine-internal profiler sees op-level behavior no host collector can observe but writes its own files, so record-owned storage and per-rank delta verification replace the managed report lifecycle for it. Engine trace is confined to local non-containerized placements because retrieval over SSH or out of a container is undefined, not because the mechanism is weaker. Binding semantic windows to stable role, replica, process, and rank targets keeps traces comparable across single-role and multi-role topologies, while static range planning preserves the Nsight Systems repeat-count behavior needed by framework-native CUDA profiler controls. The capture-armed readiness wait is unbounded because the readiness loop already fails instantly on process-group death and cleanly on interruption, so a timeout's only unique detection is the alive-but-stuck class — while the failure such a budget actually produces is a progressing instrumented warmup killed by a limit written for uninstrumented startup. Window-opening control stays fail-fast because a lost start silently shifts every later range index off its planned window identity; window-closing control defers to coverage verification because the artifacts either landed or they did not, and a late stop response must not fail a capture whose evidence exists. Escape option lists stay split between launch and start because the qualified Nsight Systems option surfaces are disjoint where it matters — trace-shaping options exist only at launch while metrics, sampling, and capture-range options exist only at start — so a single list could not be spliced correctly. Managed facts stay managed because they are the static capture plan's spine: session identity binds control actions to their target, the report lifecycle underwrites coverage verification, and capture-range mechanics carry the planned range mapping. Dedicated fields for the trace set, sampling, and context switch dissolve the default-collision problem: those managed defaults exist to be replaced, so replacement flows through a typed field instead of an option-list collision rule. The environment map is shared across every managed Nsight invocation so binary selection and runtime dependencies do not drift between launch, collection, inspection, and finalization; only the launch invocation passes that environment onward to the wrapped server.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-RECIPE-MEASUREMENT-OVERRIDES] Recipe Measurement Overrides (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-recipe-measurement-overrides"></a>

`recipe run` MUST accept invocation-scoped typed patches for Eval and Bench definitions selected by the recipe's workload suite.

An Eval patch path MUST be rooted at `evals.<eval-id>`. A Bench patch path MUST be rooted at `benches.<bench-id>`. A path naming an unselected definition MUST be rejected before the server starts.

Measurement patches MUST use the same repeatable TOML key-path and value syntax and command-order precedence as server patches in [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution).

A measurement patch MAY assign a typed optional field that the workspace declaration omitted. It MUST NOT change measurement identity or kind, workload-suite membership or order, gate selection, recipe identity, or selected server.

Each measurement child record MUST preserve the declared definition, the complete effective definition, and the ordered invocation overrides that produced it.

The framework-neutral override surface MUST NOT define a generic array append or removal language.

**Rationale:** Operators need to vary bounded sample counts and concurrency while keeping the recipe's server and measurement composition reproducible. Typed definition patches provide that iteration point without creating a second recipe or a general workflow language.

*Since: v0.8.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-LM-EVAL] lm-eval Task And Endpoint Contract (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-lm-eval"></a>

An lm-eval definition MUST select exactly one task source: one individual task name built into the release-pinned lm-eval runtime, one InferLab-bundled task selected by a `bundled` name, or one workspace-local lm-eval YAML file resolved relative to the workspace root.

A bundled task MUST resolve its task definition, prompt and dataset assets, and scorer from the bundled Eval task closure fixed by the invoking InferLab release. It MUST NOT require a downstream workspace copy or fetch task content from the network.

A workspace-local task YAML path MUST resolve to a regular file inside the workspace. The selected file and the complete closure of YAML files reached through relative or absolute `include` declarations MUST remain inside the workspace and satisfy the source-containment and identity rules of [RFC-0002:C-WORKSPACE-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-workspace-authority). Selection MUST fail before inference when the file or any included source is absent, escapes the workspace, is not identity-covered, cannot be loaded by the release-pinned lm-eval runtime, or does not resolve to exactly one named task. InferLab MUST let lm-eval own task parsing and include composition in the Python Eval integration rather than copying lm-eval task semantics into the Rust control plane.

The resolved lm-eval task configuration is the sole authority for dataset path, dataset name, evaluation split, few-shot split, prompt construction, output type, filters, metrics, scoring direction, task-internal response multiplicity, and scorer behavior. A built-in task uses the configuration shipped by the release-pinned lm-eval runtime. A bundled task uses the configuration and contained assets from the release-fixed bundled Eval task closure. A workspace-local task uses its selected YAML and contained include closure. InferLab MUST NOT maintain independent task-specific prompt, answer, parsing, or scoring rules.

The definition MAY apply bounded sample count, few-shot count, seed, generation-token limit, request concurrency, fixed trial count, and timeout where those invocation controls apply. Such invocation controls MUST NOT replace task-owned dataset, prompt, output-type, filter, metric, or scoring declarations.

Every lm-eval definition used as an InferLab measurement gate MUST declare one primary metric name, one finite pass threshold, and MAY declare one primary-metric filter. The metric, optional filter, and threshold form InferLab's gate selection and MUST NOT be passed as replacements for the task's native metric or filter declarations.

InferLab MUST resolve the selected source through the installed Eval runtime before starting inference. The resolution MUST preserve exactly one task identity, effective task configuration, and output type. A selection that resolves to zero or multiple tasks MUST fail before inference and direct the operator to compose separate Eval definitions in a recipe. Task resolution or validation failure MUST fail the measurement with task-source context.

An lm-eval definition MAY declare `trials` as a positive fixed count. When omitted, its effective value MUST be one. A trial is one logical repetition of the complete resolved Eval over the same task and sample selection.

The first repeated-trial surface MUST accept `trials` greater than one only when the resolved task uses `generate_until`, selects exactly one sample, and produces exactly one scored generation response for that sample in each trial. A task outside that shape MUST remain usable with one effective trial and MUST fail before inference when a greater trial count is requested, naming the unsupported repeated-Eval shape.

Each repeated-trial request MUST use OpenAI `n=1`. Repeated Eval MUST NOT perform prefix-cache reset or issue additional endpoint requests for scouting or warm-up. The existing fixed request-concurrency control MUST retain its existing meaning for repeated-trial requests; InferLab MUST NOT add a second trial-concurrency setting or select concurrency adaptively.

For a repeated Eval, the effective base seed MUST be the definition seed or `1234` when absent. Trial indices MUST start at one, and trial index `i` MUST use request seed `base_seed + i - 1`. InferLab MUST assign stable trial identity and effective seed before releasing that trial for request execution.

A repeated Eval's selected primary metric and optional filter MUST yield one binary per-trial score whose only valid values are `0` and `1`, with higher-is-better scoring direction. Score `1` MUST classify the completed trial as passing. Score `0` MUST classify the completed trial as non-passing. A missing or non-binary score for an otherwise completed trial MUST fail repeated-result normalization.

A repeated Eval threshold MUST be finite and within the inclusive range `[0, 1]`. At terminal result publication, `requested_trials` MUST equal `issued_trials + unissued_trials`; `issued_trials` MUST equal `completed_trials + request_failure_trials`; and `passed_trials` MUST be no greater than `completed_trials`. A requested trial becomes issued when its generation request is released for execution. An issued trial without a terminal completed classification when the Eval case reaches its terminal point MUST count as a request-failure trial.

When `issued_trials` is greater than zero, `pass_rate` MUST equal `passed_trials / issued_trials`; otherwise `pass_rate` and its metric-gate conclusion MUST be absent. An unissued trial MUST NOT enter the pass-rate denominator. Whenever `issued_trials` is greater than zero, InferLab MUST compare the observed pass rate with the declared threshold even when fewer than the requested trials completed. The aggregate metric gate MUST pass when the observed pass rate is at least the threshold and MUST otherwise fail.

A timeout or interruption of the overall repeated Eval case MUST fail that case and prevent its guarded Bench work even when the observed metric gate passed. Endpoint or task-specific non-pass classifications MAY be preserved as evidence, but the task and its scorer remain their authority.

The resolved model locator MUST be the default Hugging Face tokenizer source for the release-pinned lm-eval OpenAI client selected under RFC-0004:C-INFERENCE-REQUESTS. InferLab MUST set `tokenizer_backend=huggingface` and `tokenized_requests=false`: lm-eval uses that tokenizer for context lengths and alignment while requests remain text. The first supported surface MUST NOT introduce a second tokenizer-path authority.

A resolved task using `generate_until` MUST NOT require prompt-token log probabilities. A resolved task using `loglikelihood`, `loglikelihood_rolling`, or `multiple_choice` MUST pass the default endpoint conformance probe before evaluation starts.

The default conformance probe MUST use the exact UTF-8 prompt `Inferlab prompt logprob probe: 0123456789`. The resolved tokenizer MUST encode that prompt into at least two tokens or the probe MUST fail with tokenizer context. The probe MUST send one non-streaming request to the resolved public completions endpoint with the resolved served model, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1`, `echo=true`, and `logprobs=1`. Its tokenizer loading and HTTP operation MUST each consume the remaining Eval case budget and MUST NOT acquire a shorter fixed attempt cap.

A successful conformance probe MUST receive a 2xx JSON response with one indexed choice whose `text` is a string and whose `logprobs` object contains equal-length `tokens`, `token_logprobs`, `top_logprobs`, and `text_offset` arrays covering the echoed prompt and generated token. It MUST establish that the echoed prompt token count and text align with the resolved tokenizer. It MUST establish that prompt positions needed for continuation scoring have numeric log probabilities and top-logprob objects. It MUST establish that the generated position has a numeric log probability and top-logprob object.

The probe conclusion MUST be one of `supported`, `unsupported`, or `inconclusive`. A conforming 2xx response with generated-token logprobs but no scored prompt positions MUST conclude `unsupported`. A conforming 2xx response whose echoed prompt does not align with the resolved tokenizer MUST conclude `unsupported` for that model and route. A transport failure, timeout, non-2xx response, or malformed response MUST conclude `inconclusive` because it does not prove endpoint capability. Every conclusion other than `supported` MUST fail before lm-eval inference with an explicit typed failure. InferLab MUST NOT silently fall back from loglikelihood semantics to generation semantics.

When a primary-metric filter is declared, the native lm-eval metric key MUST match that metric and filter exactly. When no filter is declared, selection MUST succeed only when exactly one finite native metric for the declared metric name exists at the selected task result. Missing, ambiguous, non-numeric, or non-finite selections MUST fail. Result ordering, bare aliases, and single-result fallback MUST NOT choose a metric.

For an Eval with one effective trial, the primary metric MUST be selected from the one resolved task; unrelated task or aggregate results MUST NOT be substituted. The task's resolved `higher_is_better` declaration is the comparison authority: a finite selected value passes at or above the threshold when true and at or below the threshold when false. A missing or ambiguous comparison direction MUST fail the gate. For a repeated Eval, the pass-rate rules above replace that single-result comparison without replacing the task's per-trial metric or scorer.

A successful lm-eval result MUST preserve the complete raw result and a normalized finite metric map with task, native metric key, and filter provenance. A started lm-eval attempt MUST preserve its native command, terminal process outcome, stdout, stderr, raw output directory, and any partial result files even when execution, result discovery, or normalization fails.

**Rationale:** A task YAML and release-fixed task bundle are already reproducible units for dataset, prompt, output, filter, and scoring behavior, so InferLab keeps those semantics with the task rather than creating a second task language in the control plane or its RFCs. The model locator remains the tokenizer authority. A bounded prompt-logprob probe makes loglikelihood support an observed property of the complete public route. Exact metric provenance prevents successful gates from depending on map ordering or whichever filter happens to sort first. Fixed outer trials add reproducible pass-rate measurement for the demonstrated single-sample generation workflow without generalizing Eval into a workflow language or changing existing request-concurrency semantics.

*Since: v0.9.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-INFERENCE-REQUESTS] Task-Directed Inference Requests (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-inference-requests"></a>

An lm-eval or serving-Bench definition MAY declare one structured OpenAI request-body fragment in the field `request_body`.

`request_body` MUST be a TOML table that projects to a JSON object. TOML tables project recursively to JSON objects; arrays preserve order and project to JSON arrays; strings, booleans, integers, and finite floating-point values preserve their JSON scalar type. TOML date and time values MUST be rejected. TOML has no null value, so a definition or command-line override MUST NOT synthesize JSON null.

The request-body fragment MUST preserve operator-declared JSON member names, nesting, values, and scalar types. InferLab MUST NOT translate those members into a framework-neutral sampling or reasoning profile. InferLab MUST NOT silently remove a member because one backend does not support it.

An Eval or Bench definition MUST NOT expose a sibling `temperature`, reasoning, sampling, logprob, chat-template, or endpoint-selection field that duplicates a member owned by `request_body` or the resolved measurement semantics. A serving-Bench local prompt representation and any locally applied chat template MAY be declared only inside the synthetic request source prompt table governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PROMPT-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-prompt-authority); it MUST NOT be duplicated in `request_body` or exposed as an independent endpoint selector. An lm-eval prompt authority MAY be declared only inside the Eval prompt table governed by [RFC-0004:C-EVAL-PROMPT-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-eval-prompt-authority) and is subject to the same prohibition.

The resolved task and measurement runtime MUST remain authoritative for the served model, prompt or messages, stream mode, requested completion count, output-token bound, and stop conditions. A request-body fragment that declares `model`, `prompt`, `messages`, `stream`, `n`, `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, or `stop` MUST fail definition resolution and identify the conflicting member. Server-side template controls such as `chat_template` and `chat_template_kwargs` MAY remain non-structural request-body members only when the resolved task or serving-Bench prompt semantics assigns rendering to the model server. In that case they MUST be preserved under their real JSON names, and InferLab MUST claim only that those members were forwarded. A serving-Bench prompt kind whose rendering authority is local MUST reject those members rather than preserve two template authorities.

For an lm-eval definition, the resolved definition seed and repeated-trial seed schedule MUST remain authoritative for the request seed. An lm-eval `request_body` fragment that declares `seed` MUST fail definition resolution and identify that conflicting member.

A serving-Bench output-shape control is also authoritative for request members that AIPerf emits to enforce that shape. A serving-Bench `request_body` MUST reject `min_tokens`, `min_new_tokens`, and `ignore_eos` while InferLab derives those members from the declared output shape.

Request-body members supplied by a release-pinned task or measurement client are task defaults. A definition request-body fragment MAY replace a non-reserved default. Resolution MUST recursively merge object members. At the same member path, a later scalar or array replaces the earlier value atomically, and a later object recursively merges with an earlier object. Traversing a nested override through a non-object value MUST fail and identify that path.

The precedence order MUST be release-pinned task or client defaults, definition `request_body`, then invocation-scoped overrides in command-line order. The resolved evidence MUST retain an overridden default, its replacement, and their authority sources.

Every request emitted for an Eval or Bench attempt MUST request exactly one completion.

Each lm-eval definition MUST resolve to exactly one individual lm-eval task. A selection that resolves to zero or multiple tasks MUST fail before inference and identify that the operator must select each task as a separate Eval definition in a recipe.

lm-eval prompt authority, its declaration domain, the derived protocol route, and the derived native client MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-EVAL-PROMPT-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-eval-prompt-authority).

The resolved model locator MUST be the sole tokenizer source for serving-Bench generation, local prompt-length projection, and pre-template content-token measurement. The Bench runtime MUST load it locally with the Hugging Face tokenizer backend fixed by the release-pinned Bench toolchain. A Bench definition MUST NOT declare another tokenizer locator, revision, or backend. The resolved execution MUST preserve the model locator, tokenizer backend, and installed Transformers version.

Serving-Bench synthetic prompt authority, request representation, selected input-token meaning, exactness policy, and derived AIPerf route MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PROMPT-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-prompt-authority). Dataset-backed independent requests and every linear-session turn on the valid path through its first failure MUST retain structured messages and server rendering. A native linear-session turn emitted after that failure is retained only as failure evidence and is not required to contain a missing assistant response.

For dataset request sources, admission and source-shape evidence MUST measure the sum of structured message-content token lengths with `add_special_tokens=false`. Server-added template tokens are outside the source admission bound. Native AIPerf request artifacts remain authoritative for the structured messages actually sent, and backend-reported profiling `prompt_tokens` remains authoritative for the observed post-template input length.

The resolved prompt representation, rendering authority, and derived route MUST be one frozen authority used by dry-run, population preparation, execution, and records. The request form MUST NOT be exposed as an independent operator-selected endpoint switch.

The built-in OpenAI smoke MUST use the declared completions path and MUST NOT consume a definition request-body fragment.

A serving-Bench `server_chat` attempt MUST fail with the backend diagnostic context when the selected model has no usable server-side chat template. InferLab MUST NOT switch prompt kind or fall back to completions after that failure.

A request-body fragment belongs to its one Eval task or serving-Bench definition. Operators compose multiple tasks as separate Eval definitions in a recipe, so each task retains an explicit request fragment and route.

Invocation-scoped measurement overrides MUST address `evals.<eval-id>.request_body.<path>` or `benches.<bench-id>.request_body.<path>`. They MUST use the precedence, declared-definition, effective-definition, and ordered-override evidence rules in RFC-0004:C-RECIPE-MEASUREMENT-OVERRIDES.

The selected named path and complete effective `request_body` fragment MUST be fixed before the native measurement client starts. The client MUST apply that fragment to every real request body after task or client defaults and before transport. Dynamic task-owned prompt or message content remains part of the measurement engine's native sample or request artifacts rather than a fabricated single body for a multi-request attempt. Evidence MUST satisfy RFC-0005:C-INFERENCE-REQUEST-EVIDENCE.

**Rationale:** The OpenAI request is the backend-visible experiment input. Preserving a body fragment directly supports evolving framework fields such as `temperature`, `logprobs`, and `reasoning_effort` without creating a lossy InferLab parameter language. Task and prompt semantics retain authority for structural request members, rendering, and route selection; the route is derived rather than independently configured. Recipe-level composition keeps multi-task experiments explicit without requiring per-task routing inside one lm-eval invocation.

*Since: v0.11.1*

### [RFC-0004:C-EVAL-PROMPT-AUTHORITY] Generative Eval Prompt Authority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-eval-prompt-authority"></a>

An lm-eval definition whose resolved task output type is `generate_until` MAY declare one prompt table whose `kind` is `flat` or `server_chat`. Omission of that table MUST resolve to `flat`. An lm-eval definition whose resolved task output type is `loglikelihood`, `loglikelihood_rolling`, or `multiple_choice`, or whose resolved task does not reduce to one request type, MUST NOT declare that table and MUST resolve to `flat`, because the release-pinned lm-eval chat client does not implement loglikelihood scoring, so a task that emits any loglikelihood request cannot place any of its requests on the chat route.

`flat` MUST use the declared completions path with the release-pinned lm-eval `local-completions` client and MUST NOT enable lm-eval structured chat construction. The task-owned context therefore crosses as ordinary text and the resolved task retains the continuation and scoring format its filters expect.

`server_chat` MUST use the declared chat-completions path with the release-pinned lm-eval `local-chat-completions` client and MUST enable lm-eval structured chat construction so task context becomes a message list before request lowering. With `tokenized_requests=false`, InferLab MUST let the model server apply its model-owned chat template and MUST NOT locally render those messages into a completion prompt.

The resolved prompt authority MUST determine one protocol route and one native client. An independent operator-selected endpoint switch MUST NOT permit a second route choice, and InferLab MUST NOT derive the authority from a task identity table it owns.

Server-side template controls such as `chat_template` and `chat_template_kwargs` MAY remain non-structural `request_body` members only under `server_chat`. Under `flat` they MUST fail definition resolution and identify the conflicting member. That legality MUST be evaluated against the effective prompt authority after invocation-scoped overrides, so an override that changes the authority also changes which request-body members are legal.

A `server_chat` attempt MUST fail with the backend diagnostic context when the selected model has no usable server-side chat template. InferLab MUST NOT switch prompt authority or fall back to completions after that failure.

The resolved prompt authority, the derived route, and the derived native client MUST be fixed before the native measurement client starts and MUST be recorded with the effective Eval definition. Records MUST distinguish a declared authority from a defaulted one. Native sample evidence MUST preserve the effective task context or messages that lm-eval exposes. A reported Eval metric MUST NOT be presented without its resolved prompt authority, because the same task scored under a different authority is a different measurement. Evidence MUST satisfy RFC-0005:C-INFERENCE-REQUEST-EVIDENCE.

**Rationale:** Chat rendering and continuation scoring are different evaluation workloads, not two spellings of one request. A task whose filters expect its demonstration continuation format loses accuracy under server chat rendering, while a task or model whose behavior depends on the model chat template and its reasoning controls needs that rendering. Defaulting an omitted authority to `flat` runs the resolved task in the form its own demonstrations and filters were authored for, so InferLab interposes no rendering unless an operator asks for it; the deviation is declared, not the baseline. Because the choice still moves a metric that a definition compares against a threshold and a recipe can use as a gate, records separate a declared authority from a defaulted one, and InferLab derives the default from one fixed rule rather than from a task table it maintains. The remaining output types declare nothing because the release-pinned client implements no alternative for them.

*Since: v0.28.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-SLO] Serving Bench SLO And Adaptive Rate Search (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-slo"></a>

A static or adaptive serving-Bench definition MAY declare the ordered field `aggregate_slos` as a non-empty list of constraints over stable InferLab Bench metrics governed by [RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-measurements) or this clause.

Each aggregate constraint MUST name one known stable metric and MUST declare exactly one finite inclusive bound, `at_most` or `at_least`.

All declared aggregate constraints MUST pass for a case to satisfy its aggregate SLOs.

An aggregate TPOT constraint MUST fail definition resolution when the selected request source makes TPOT inapplicable.

The metrics `good_request_ratio` and `goodput` MUST be valid aggregate-constraint metrics only when the same definition declares a request-level SLO.

An unavailable `prompt_cache_read_ratio` MUST produce an `unavailable` aggregate-constraint outcome that does not satisfy that constraint without invalidating an otherwise complete measurement.

A configured distribution metric that has no completed-request population MUST produce an `unavailable` aggregate-constraint outcome that does not satisfy that constraint when a request-level SLO measurement is otherwise complete and internally consistent.

A missing, non-numeric, or non-finite value for any other configured aggregate metric that should exist for the observed profiling population MUST invalidate the measurement result.

A static or adaptive serving-Bench definition MAY declare one `request_slo` containing optional inclusive upper bounds `request_latency_ms`, `ttft_ms`, and `tpot_ms`, plus the required field `minimum_good_request_ratio`.

A request-level SLO MUST declare at least one request-metric upper bound.

Every request-metric upper bound MUST be finite and non-negative.

`minimum_good_request_ratio` MUST be finite and greater than zero and less than or equal to one.

A request-level `tpot_ms` bound MUST fail definition resolution when the selected request source makes TPOT inapplicable.

InferLab MUST lower the request-level bounds to the release-pinned AIPerf runtime without exposing AIPerf's arbitrary SLO-tag surface as InferLab definition fields.

A profiling request MUST count as good only when it terminates without error or cancellation, supplies every request metric required by the definition, and satisfies every declared request-metric upper bound.

An errored request, cancelled request, or completed request missing a required request metric MUST count as not good.

The AIPerf native per-request metrics export for the profiling phase MUST be the file-bound authority for attempted, completed, failed, and good request counts used by request-level SLO evaluation.

Each exported profiling record MUST carry its native `session_num` transport-request identity, and those identities MUST be unique within the profiling phase. Independent-request population reconciliation follows [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-request-sources); linear-session identity and turn reconciliation follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSIONS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-linear-sessions).

The export MUST contain exactly the resolved profiling request count frozen in the case before launch. A missing or duplicate request identity, a non-terminal profiling record, or a terminal-record count that differs from that resolved count MUST invalidate the measurement.

Each terminal profiling record without an error or cancellation MUST count as completed.

Each terminal profiling record with an error or cancellation MUST count as failed.

The attempted-request denominator MUST equal the resolved profiling request count, the number of unique terminal profiling records, and completed requests plus failed requests.

For a completed profiling record that supplies every request metric required by the definition, its native per-request `good_request_count` value MUST be present, integral, and either zero or one, and MUST be the authority for whether that request is good. A value of one MUST be invalid when any required request metric is absent.

A completed profiling record that observably lacks at least one required request metric MAY omit its native per-request `good_request_count` value and MUST count as not good. An errored or cancelled record MUST count as not good without fabricating request metrics or a good marker.

The case `good_request_count` MUST equal the sum of the valid per-request native good values; records governed as not good above contribute zero. When AIPerf emits an aggregate `good_request_count`, it MUST be integral, MUST equal that file-bound sum, and MUST lie in the inclusive range from zero through completed requests. The aggregate value MAY be absent.

The profiling duration MUST equal the maximum `request_end_ns` minus the minimum `request_start_ns` across all terminal native profiling records, converted from nanoseconds to seconds.

The profiling duration MUST be positive and finite, and its stable source identity MUST be `native-profiling-request-window`.

`good_request_ratio` MUST equal good requests divided by attempted requests.

`goodput` MUST equal good requests divided by the profiling duration and MUST use requests per second.

InferLab MUST derive `good_request_ratio` and `goodput` from those file-bound counts and duration instead of depending on optional AIPerf derived-summary fields.

A request-level SLO result MUST satisfy its ratio requirement only when `good_request_ratio` is greater than or equal to `minimum_good_request_ratio`.

A request-level SLO measurement MUST be invalid when no profiling request is attempted, a profiling record is non-terminal or malformed, or its counts, timestamps, duration, ratio, or goodput are missing, non-finite where applicable, or internally inconsistent.

An independent-request case with a request-level SLO MUST remain a successful measurement when one or more profiling requests fail, including when every attempted request fails, if the profiling phase and native per-request export are complete and internally consistent and no timeout, interruption, launch, protocol, or export failure occurred.

For an independent-request case, a non-zero AIPerf exit caused solely by every profiling request returning an inference error MUST remain service-quality evidence rather than a measurement failure when the preceding completeness conditions hold, and its native exit outcome MUST remain recorded.

A case without a request-level SLO MUST retain the existing requirement for at least one completed profiling request and zero failed profiling requests.

Measurement status MUST describe execution and result integrity independently of SLO satisfaction.

Each successfully measured case MUST evaluate every declared aggregate and request-level SLO and MUST expose one case-level SLO conclusion formed by AND across those evaluations.

A static Bench MUST execute every resolved case despite an earlier case's SLO failure.

A static Bench with SLOs MUST pass only when every resolved case executes successfully and satisfies its case-level SLO conclusion.

A static Bench without SLOs MUST retain its existing execution-success pass meaning.

An adaptive serving-Bench definition MUST declare one or more aggregate constraints, a request-level SLO, or both.

An adaptive serving-Bench definition MUST declare non-empty positive finite `initial_request_rates`, non-negative integer `max_search_steps`, and an optional positive finite `min_rate_resolution`.

`max_search_steps` MUST bound the total automatically added doubling and bisection probes after all distinct initial request rates have been probed.

The fields `target_metric`, `target_threshold`, and `max_refinement_steps` MUST NOT remain accepted adaptive-serving definition fields.

The adaptive policy identity MUST be `highest-feasible-rate-v1`.

The policy MUST probe all declared initial rates in ascending unique order unless a measurement failure, timeout, or interruption aborts the search.

The policy MUST classify a finite observed failure of only `at_least` constraints as below the feasible region.

The policy MUST classify any finite observed `at_most` failure or request-level ratio failure as above the feasible region.

The policy MUST classify a probe as feasible only when every configured aggregate and request-level SLO passes.

An unavailable aggregate constraint MUST make its probe infeasible but MUST NOT supply directional evidence for an automatically added probe.

After the initial probes, the policy MUST double the highest observed rate while that rate is feasible or has only below-region failures and no higher observed above-region rate bounds it, until it observes such a higher above-region rate or exhausts `max_search_steps`.

When automatically added bisection is possible, the active lower endpoint MUST be the highest observed rate classified as feasible or below-region that has a higher observed above-region rate.

The active upper endpoint MUST be the lowest observed above-region rate greater than that lower endpoint.

This one tightest observed bracket MUST take precedence over automatic doubling.

The next bisection probe MUST be the arithmetic midpoint of the active endpoints.

A feasible or below-region midpoint MUST replace the lower endpoint for subsequent bisection, while an above-region midpoint MUST replace the upper endpoint.

A feasible midpoint MUST additionally remain eligible for final rate selection.

The policy MUST NOT execute a midpoint already present in the observation set.

The policy MUST stop adding probes when `max_search_steps` is exhausted, when an active bracket width is less than or equal to a configured `min_rate_resolution`, or when no distinct directional probe can be derived.

The policy MUST NOT automatically probe below the lowest declared initial request rate.

The initial rates SHOULD include a low-rate anchor expected to remain below any overload boundary.

The policy MUST select the highest observed feasible rate and MUST NOT extrapolate an unmeasured rate.

The policy MUST report whether the selected rate has a higher observed above-region boundary.

Exhausting `max_search_steps` without a higher above-region observation MUST remain a normally completed search and MUST NOT claim that the selected rate is a saturation limit.

A normally completed adaptive Bench MUST pass only when it selects an observed feasible rate.

A complete probe whose request failures reduce its request-level ratio MUST remain a valid infeasible observation and MUST NOT abort adaptive search.

A probe whose launch, timeout, interruption, protocol, native-artifact, or required-result validation fails MUST abort adaptive search as a measurement failure and MUST NOT be treated as above-region evidence, except for the complete all-inference-error outcome governed above.

The policy MUST describe its result as the highest observed feasible rate under the executed probes and MUST NOT claim a global optimum across unobserved rates or non-contiguous feasible regions.

Manual and closed-loop execution MUST apply the same resolved SLO evaluation and adaptive policy for the same effective Bench definition and serving snapshot.

**Rationale:** Serving operators need both distribution-level limits and the rate of individually good requests. Under the ordinary serving regime, throughput floors and latency or quality ceilings form an approximately contiguous feasible-rate interval; deterministic doubling plus directional bisection finds useful observed boundaries without importing a general optimizer or claiming statistical certainty that the measurements do not provide.

*Since: v0.15.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES] Serving Bench Request Sources (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-request-sources"></a>

A serving-Bench definition that selects independent requests MUST declare one `request_source` table whose `kind` is `random`, `random_mixture`, `dataset`, or `replay`. A definition that selects dependent linear sessions MUST instead follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSIONS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-linear-sessions); a definition that selects recorded agentic session trees MUST instead follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-AGENTIC-TRACE-REPLAY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-agentic-trace-replay). The former top-level `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` fields MUST be rejected rather than retained as a compatibility representation.

A `random` request source MUST declare `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`. Each token-length selector MUST be either a positive integer, meaning one fixed value, or a table with positive integer `min` and `max` fields whose `min` is strictly less than its `max`. Such a table MAY omit `kind`; omission MUST resolve to `inclusive_uniform`. When the table declares `kind`, its value MUST be `inclusive_uniform`. Both forms MUST resolve to the same canonical inclusive-uniform selector identity in merged workspace output, dry-run, execution, and record evidence. Other distributions, ratio shorthands, means, standard deviations, and unbounded ranges MUST be rejected.

For every generated entry, InferLab MUST sample the input and output selectors independently. An `inclusive_uniform` selector MUST assign equal probability to every integer from `min` through `max`, inclusive. The Bench seed and selector identity MUST determine the sequence, and generating a larger population MUST preserve the same first N selected pairs.

For `random` and `random_mixture`, the selected input-token target and synthetic prompt materialization MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PROMPT-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-prompt-authority). The effective output-token value MUST be the exact requested output-token limit. A fixed output value of one MUST remain valid for the existing prefill-dominant workflow. An output selector whose possible values include both one and values of at least two MUST be rejected so one Bench retains one unambiguous normalized metric schema.

A `random` request source MAY declare one `corpus` table whose `path` is a workspace-relative path to an operator-supplied text corpus and whose optional `expected_sha256` binds the corpus bytes. The same locator rules as the replay population file apply: the path MUST NOT be absolute and MUST NOT escape the workspace, and a declared digest MUST match the observed corpus bytes before preparation completes. Corpus content MUST NOT be supplied inline or through a remote reference. An invocation override MUST NOT change the corpus `path` or `expected_sha256`.

When `corpus` is declared, entry content MUST be drawn from the corpus instead of the synthetic word supply. InferLab MUST tokenize the corpus once with the resolved model tokenizer, and each entry MUST take exactly its selected input-token target as one slice of the corpus token stream whose offset is determined by the Bench seed and the entry's population index alone, decoded back to text under the same round-trip verification as synthetic prompts. The offset MUST NOT depend on the total population size, so generating a larger population MUST preserve the same first N selected entries. A corpus whose token stream is shorter than the largest selected input-token target MUST fail preparation.

Corpus slices MUST be drawn independently and MAY overlap. Incidental sharing between overlapping slices is natural reuse: it MUST NOT be measured, promised, or presented as controlled prefix geometry. A declared `prefix_sharing` MUST retain its exact controlled semantics, with the shared prefix taken as one fixed corpus slice and each unique suffix drawn independently. Omission of `corpus` MUST resolve to the synthetic word supply with unchanged semantics.

A dry-run MUST resolve the corpus path, declared and observed digest state, and the corpus token length when the corpus bytes and tokenizer are locally available, without fabricating population facts.

The frozen population MUST preserve each entry's selected input- and output-token targets. A configured selector describes target request shapes, not the realized output length returned by the server.

Synthetic shared-prefix declarations and their lowering MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PREFIX-GEOMETRY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-prefix-geometry). Omission declares no controlled shared-prefix geometry; it MUST NOT be interpreted as a promised zero cache-hit outcome.

A `random_mixture` request source MUST declare at least two ordered, distinct `shapes`. Each shape MUST declare positive exact `input_tokens`, positive exact requested `output_tokens`, and a positive unsigned 32-bit integer `weight`. Its token lengths MUST have the same complete prompt-target and requested output-limit meanings as `random`. Two shapes with the same input- and output-token lengths MUST be rejected. The checked sum of weights MUST fit an unsigned 64-bit integer.

For each generated mixture entry, InferLab MUST select one shape independently with replacement from the categorical distribution whose probability is `shape.weight / sum(shape.weight)`. The Bench seed and ordered shape list MUST determine the selection sequence, and generating a larger population MUST preserve the same first N selections. Weights MUST NOT be presented as exact realized request quotas.

All shapes in one `random_mixture` MUST declare `output_tokens` equal to one, or all shapes MUST declare `output_tokens` of at least two. A mixture spanning those two TPOT applicability classes MUST be rejected so one Bench retains one unambiguous normalized metric schema. Each generated entry MUST materialize according to its resolved prompt kind and selected input-token target under [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PROMPT-AUTHORITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-prompt-authority).

For each effective random source and Bench seed, InferLab MUST define one logical deterministic entry sequence. Every static case and adaptive probe MUST independently instantiate that sequence and consume its prefix of the resolved warmup-plus-profiling length. Within a case, warmup MUST consume the first resolved warmup entries and profiling MUST consume the immediately following entries. The sequence MUST NOT wrap, and one generated entry MUST produce exactly one independent transport request.

A `dataset` request source MUST declare a release-qualified `dataset` name and positive `max_input_tokens`. It MAY declare a release-qualified `profile` name and positive `output_tokens` as a fixed override. A catalog entry MAY require a profile and MUST define its closed valid profile set. Omission of `output_tokens` MUST derive each request's output-token limit from its held-out assistant target only for catalog entries that provide such targets.

The Bench-level `seed` MUST remain the authority for request-source randomness and the existing stochastic load behavior. An invocation override MUST NOT change `request_source.kind`.

A dataset name MUST resolve through the catalog fixed by the invoking InferLab release. The definition MUST NOT supply an arbitrary source URL, repository, revision, local path, data format, loader, or AIPerf dataset type.

Each catalog entry MUST bind one stable name to one immutable upstream snapshot, expected SHA-256 digest, source format, and versioned materialization semantics. A profiled catalog entry MUST additionally bind each stable profile name to one source split and closed filter policy. A release MUST NOT resolve one catalog or profile name to different source bytes or selection semantics.

The release-qualified catalog MUST provide `speed_bench` profiles backed by an immutable NVIDIA SPEED-Bench snapshot.
