Its profile set MUST distinguish supported qualitative categories and supported throughput input-length and entropy subsets without accepting an arbitrary category, split, Hugging Face selector, or AIPerf plugin name. A `speed_bench` request source MUST declare a profile and fixed `output_tokens`.

`toolchain install` MUST NOT acquire catalog dataset bytes. Before executing a Bench that selects a dataset source, InferLab MUST resolve the catalog entry and make its verified source snapshot available before the first transport request.

A missing source snapshot MUST be downloaded with operator-visible progress. The downloaded bytes MUST match the catalog digest before InferLab publishes them to the cache. A download, transport, or digest failure MUST fail dataset preparation without starting the measurement client.

The source cache MUST use `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/inferlab/datasets/sha256/<digest>`, with the conventional `$HOME/.cache` default when `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is unset. A verified cache hit MUST avoid network access. The cache MUST remain machine-local, recoverable state and MUST NOT be placed in a workspace or versioned toolchain prefix.

Dataset materialization MUST use the resolved model tokenizer governed by [RFC-0004:C-INFERENCE-REQUESTS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-inference-requests) to measure each input as the sum of its structured message-content token lengths before server chat-template rendering. It MUST preserve the source messages as structured roles and content. Every admitted independent entry MUST remain structured messages for the pinned AIPerf chat endpoint; InferLab MUST NOT freeze a flat prompt or apply a chat template in the measurement runtime.

For a source conversation ending in an assistant target, materialization MUST first treat every preceding message through the last user message as one candidate request and hold out the assistant target. When that candidate exceeds `max_input_tokens`, materialization MUST remove one complete trailing user-and-assistant exchange and retry with the preceding assistant target. It MUST NOT drop leading history, truncate message content, or leave an assistant message as the final input message.

A conversation for which no non-empty user input and assistant target fit MUST be ineligible. When output length is dataset-derived, an assistant target shorter than two tokenizer tokens MUST be ineligible so TPOT remains defined for every admitted request. A fixed `output_tokens` override MUST replace the target-derived length and MAY be one.

For a `speed_bench` `request_source` profile, catalog materialization MUST map the first non-empty upstream `turns` element to exactly one structured message whose role is `user` and whose content is that turn's unchanged string. That message MUST produce one independent chat-completions request without client rendering. Materialization MUST NOT replay later turns or expose the AIPerf loader's multi-turn default in this RFC version. A row with no non-empty first user turn or whose first-turn input exceeds `max_input_tokens` before template rendering MUST be ineligible; materialization MUST NOT truncate it.

For a `speed_bench` `request_source`, AIPerf MUST consume the frozen population through its release-pinned dataset and reporting boundary. InferLab MUST NOT invoke a vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or other serving-framework benchmark client for that population.

Within `request_source`, one admitted dataset sample MUST produce exactly one independent transport request. Prior assistant messages in that request MUST come from the source snapshot. InferLab and AIPerf MUST NOT replay source turns as a stateful multi-request session.

InferLab MUST deterministically order candidate samples from the definition seed, select without replacement, and materialize enough admitted entries for the largest resolved warmup-plus-profiling population required by the Bench. Every case MUST consume a prefix of that one frozen population. Warmup and profiling within a case MUST consume disjoint sequential entries.

When the source cannot provide the required admitted population, preparation MUST fail before the first case. InferLab MUST NOT repeat or oversample entries to fill the deficit. AIPerf MUST consume the frozen materialized population sequentially and MUST NOT fetch, reshuffle, resample, or wrap the source.

A dry-run MUST resolve the catalog identity, request-source policy, cache path, and observed cache state without downloading missing bytes. When the verified source and tokenizer inputs are already available, dry-run SHOULD report the same determinable materialized-population facts as execution. A cache miss MUST be reported as a planned acquisition rather than fabricated population evidence.

A `replay` request source MUST declare a workspace-relative `path` naming a population file in the release's materialized population format and MUST declare its `prompt` kind. It MAY declare `expected_sha256`; when declared, preparation MUST verify that the file content digest matches before any transport request. The file content MUST be the sole population authority: entry order, subset selection, duplication, and content edits are expressed by the file itself, and InferLab MUST NOT offer selection, filtering, or transformation of a replay source.

A replay source MUST NOT declare token-length selectors or output overrides; each entry's recorded input- and output-token targets remain authoritative. Entries mixing the output-one and output-at-least-two TPOT applicability classes MUST be rejected, as for generated sources.

A replay source MAY declare `prefix_sharing`; its geometry MUST be resolved from the file entries, and cache-state conditioning MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state) unchanged. Downstream of population preparation, a replayed population MUST be indistinguishable from a generated one: every case consumes a prefix of the replayed sequence, warmup and profiling consume disjoint sequential entries, and an insufficient population MUST fail preparation without repeating entries.

Preparation MUST validate each entry against the declared prompt kind and the materialized format. A missing file, digest mismatch, malformed entry, or prompt-shape mismatch MUST fail preparation before the first transport request. An invocation override MUST NOT change the replay `path` or `expected_sha256`.

A dry-run MUST resolve the path, declared and observed digest state, prompt kind, and entry count without fabricating population facts.

**Rationale:** Fixed random shapes, weighted exact-shape mixtures, controlled final-prompt prefix geometry, server-rendered shared-content compatibility, and bounded conversational data are demonstrated request-origin workflows with distinct validation rules but the same serving measurement lifecycle. A closed request source makes those rules explicit while preserving one load, warmup, SLO, timeout, and evidence path. Shared geometry controls reproducible input construction without promising a backend-dependent cache-hit outcome. Relative shape weights expose a realistic mixed workload without promoting the open AIPerf distribution language. Release-qualified source identity and control-plane acquisition keep network behavior and reproducibility visible without exposing the AIPerf dataset surface. Tail rollback preserves a real conversation prefix; deterministic sampling without replacement avoids artificial prefix-cache reuse. An optional corpus declaration replaces only the content supply of the random source so content-sensitive measurements such as speculative-decoding acceptance rates run on natural-language prompts while population geometry stays release-owned.

*Since: v0.16.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSIONS] Serving Bench Linear Sessions (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-linear-sessions"></a>

A static `serving` Bench definition MAY declare `session_source`. A session source represents a frozen population of dependent linear conversation templates, not independent transport requests, and MUST NOT expose AIPerf dataset, loader, scenario, context-mode, or plugin names.

A `session_source` MUST declare a release-qualified `dataset` and positive `max_input_tokens`. It MAY declare a release-qualified `profile` and positive fixed `output_tokens`. It MAY declare finite non-negative `inter_turn_delay_scale`, which defaults to `1.0`, and finite non-negative `max_inter_turn_delay_seconds`; omission of the maximum means that no cap applies. A typed invocation override MAY change either delay control within the selected session-source boundary. The catalog, immutable snapshot, acquisition, cache, tokenizer, structured-message routing, and dry-run rules of [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-request-sources) apply. The selected catalog entry MUST define versioned linear-template materialization and whether every source turn has a held-out assistant target from which to derive its output-token limit. Omitting `output_tokens` MUST be rejected when any admitted turn lacks such a target.

A linear-session definition MUST declare `session_source` and MUST reject `request_source` and `agentic_source`. A session-backed definition MUST declare non-empty positive `concurrency`, positive `sessions_per_concurrency`, and MAY declare non-negative `warmup_sessions_per_concurrency`, which defaults to zero. It MUST reject `prompts_per_concurrency`, `warmup_prompts_per_concurrency`, `request_rates`, `request_count`, `duration_seconds`, and `burstiness`. `adaptive-serving` MUST reject `session_source`, and invocation overrides MUST NOT change the selected source boundary.

For concurrency `c`, the profiling and warmup session counts MUST be `c * sessions_per_concurrency` and `c * warmup_sessions_per_concurrency`. An unrepresentable count MUST fail resolution. Concurrency is the maximum number of active native conversations: a session occupies one slot from first-turn admission until its final planned native turn returns or the phase terminates, including while an inter-turn delay or post-failure continuation elapses, and has at most one request in flight. InferLab MUST adjudicate success from the first failing turn without treating that adjudication point as slot release. The phase MUST admit frozen templates in order whenever a native slot is available until the resolved session count has started.

A linear template MUST have one stable template identity and at least two ordered source turns. The supported catalog materialization MUST consist only of those source turns and MUST NOT add a separate system message. Each turn MUST have one non-empty structured user message and one positive requested output-token limit. A turn after the first MAY have finite non-negative `inter_turn_delay_seconds`, which is the source think time before that turn; omission resolves to zero. A catalog materializer that derives this value from recorded timing MUST use the idle interval from the preceding source response's terminal receipt to the current source request's start. It MUST NOT treat a request-start-to-request-start interval as post-response think time. A source trajectory in which the current request starts before the preceding response terminates MUST NOT be admitted as a linear template. A template MUST NOT contain an executable branch, tool step, replayable source assistant turn, or model-selected action.

For every turn after the first, InferLab MUST multiply the source `inter_turn_delay_seconds` by the effective `inter_turn_delay_scale` and, when `max_inter_turn_delay_seconds` is declared, cap that product at the declared maximum. The resulting effective delay MUST be finite and non-negative; an unrepresentable result MUST fail materialization. These controls MUST NOT synthesize a delay distribution, reorder turns, or incorporate live inference latency. The effective controls and delays MUST contribute to the frozen population identity.

A fixed `output_tokens` value MUST replace every target-derived turn limit. Otherwise a held-out assistant target MAY determine only that turn limit; its content MUST NOT enter runtime history, and a template containing a target shorter than two tokenizer tokens MUST be ineligible. A fixed value of one makes TPOT inapplicable to the population; every other admitted population makes TPOT applicable. A template whose first pre-template content-token count exceeds `max_input_tokens` MUST be ineligible and MUST NOT be truncated.

InferLab MUST deterministically order eligible templates from the Bench seed and catalog materialization identity and freeze enough for the largest resolved warmup-plus-profiling population before the first case. Cases MUST use prefixes of that population; warmup and profiling within a case MUST use disjoint sequential slices. Selection MUST be without replacement or wrap, and insufficient eligible templates MUST fail preparation.

Each admitted template instance MUST receive one `x_correlation_id` unique within the complete Bench execution, which is the runtime session identity used by InferLab and AIPerf. The template identity remains separate, and a turn identity is the runtime session identity plus its zero-based source-turn index. All turns MUST use the case-resolved chat-completions route, model, structured-message representation, and request fragment. Propagating `x_correlation_id` MUST NOT be presented as backend routing affinity unless the resolved serving capability establishes that fact.

Turn zero MUST contain the first source user message. On the valid path through the first session failure, turn `n > 0` MUST begin only after turn `n - 1` returns a valid live assistant response and the effective inter-turn delay, measured from terminal response receipt, has elapsed. Its history MUST contain every preceding source-user and live-assistant pair followed by source user message `n`. Source assistant targets MUST NOT replace live responses, and turns from one session MUST NOT overlap. A native turn emitted after an invalid predecessor belongs only to failed-session evidence, is not required to contain the missing assistant response, and cannot satisfy this dependency.

The frozen first turn MUST satisfy `max_input_tokens` before the measurement client starts. For every attempted turn, InferLab MUST measure the pre-template content-token count from the native structured-message request as the sum of tokenizer lengths of all message content with `add_special_tokens=false`. The count includes source-user and live-assistant content and excludes roles, server template delimiters, and the generation prompt. Because AIPerf owns dependent-turn dispatch, a later turn that exceeds `max_input_tokens` MAY already have reached the server; it MUST fail session adjudication, MUST preserve the native request and backend outcome, and MUST NOT be presented as a successful bounded session. InferLab MUST NOT drop, truncate, replace, or locally render the history.

A transport error or cancellation, malformed or missing terminal response, missing assistant text, model-selected action payload, or content-bound violation MUST fail the session at its first affected turn. A native request emitted after that failing turn MUST remain failure evidence and MUST NOT restore session or case success. Other sessions MAY continue under AIPerf scheduling. A session succeeds only after every planned turn returns a valid text-only assistant response without a bound violation. A case deadline, interruption, client failure, or cleanup cancellation MUST fail affected sessions and preserve partial evidence.

A positive warmup session count MUST use a complete AIPerf-native session-bounded warmup phase with the same source-population policy, route, served model, request fragment, and dependent-session construction as profiling. The AIPerf-native phase marker allowed by RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS MAY add or prepend a warmup-only system message at transport time; this is not a catalog-materialized source turn, MUST be preserved in the phase-tagged native request artifact, and contributes to the warmup request's observed prompt-token count. Warmup MUST drain before profiling, use distinct session identities and population entries, and fail the case if any warmup session is unsuccessful or missing. Warmup traffic MUST be excluded from profiling metrics. Server-metric collection during a session warmup MUST follow the profiling-window exclusion requirements in [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state).

The frozen profiling slice MUST determine planned session count and planned transport-request count, where the latter is the sum of template turn counts. Existing normalized latency, token, cache, throughput, and request-level SLO metrics retain transport-request semantics; `request_throughput` is not session throughput, and native `session_num` is a phase-local transport-request identity despite its name, and only the pair of benchmark phase and `session_num` is case-unique. A session-backed case succeeds only when every planned session succeeds, every planned turn has one terminal native request record, and all identities and counts reconcile. SLO evaluation occurs only after that completeness check, and the independent-request all-inference-error exception does not apply.

Only fixed linear source turns are supported. Executable environments, tool use, and source- or model-directed next actions require a separate contract.

**Rationale:** A linear session is a distinct load unit whose later requests depend on live responses. Source think time plus two scalar controls preserves trace shape, permits explicit compression or removal, and bounds long tails without importing AIPerf configuration or synthetic-delay models. One template identity, one runtime session identity, and native per-request evidence are sufficient to keep session scheduling and request metrics separate.

*Since: v0.18.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PROMPT-AUTHORITY] Serving Bench Prompt Authority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-prompt-authority"></a>

A `random` or `random_mixture` Bench request source MAY declare one prompt table whose `kind` is `flat`, `rendered_chat`, or `server_chat`. Omission of that table MUST resolve to `flat`. A `dataset` request source and a dependent linear session MUST NOT declare that table and MUST resolve to `server_chat`. The resolved prompt authority MUST determine one protocol route and MUST be recorded with the effective Bench definition; independent endpoint selectors MUST NOT permit a second route choice. `flat` MUST synthesize ordinary text prompts on the completions route and MUST treat the sampled input-token count as the final transport-prompt target. `rendered_chat` MUST synthesize text content, place it in a declared message template, render that conversation locally using an explicit model chat-template authority, and submit the frozen rendered prompt on the completions route; exact token-length construction MUST apply to that final rendered prompt. `server_chat` MUST submit declared messages on the chat-completions route and delegate template rendering to the server. Under `server_chat`, the sampled input-token count MUST constrain message-content tokens before server rendering; implementations SHOULD use tokenizer metadata returned by the serving integration to compensate for fixed template overhead when that overhead is known exactly, MUST fall back to uncompensated content-token control when it cannot establish that overhead, and MUST record which accounting mode was used and why. Successful requests MUST retain the backend-observed input-token count when the endpoint reports it. Failure to load an explicit local template authority, deterministic rendering failure, or inability to construct the requested final rendered length MUST fail before measurement rather than silently selecting another prompt authority.

Rationale: Message semantics and final-token shape are different workload authorities. Defaulting an omitted synthetic prompt authority to `flat` makes declared input-token targets exact by default without hiding a model- or server-specific chat template. Server rendering remains explicit when production chat behavior is itself the workload, while datasets and live histories retain it by construction. Freezing either flat text or a locally rendered chat prompt gives controlled synthetic measurements one exact transport prompt without exposing protocol paths as independent experiment controls.

*Since: v0.24.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PREFIX-GEOMETRY] Serving Bench Prefix Geometry (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-prefix-geometry"></a>

A `random` or `random_mixture` source whose prompt kind is `flat` or `rendered_chat` MAY declare one `prefix_sharing` table. That table MUST contain exactly one of `shared_prefix_tokens` or `shared_prefix_ratio`.

`shared_prefix_tokens` MUST be a non-negative integer no greater than the minimum possible selected input-token target. For every population entry it MUST resolve directly to that same shared-prefix token count.

`shared_prefix_ratio` MUST be finite and lie in the inclusive range from zero through one. For an entry with selected input-token target `I`, it MUST resolve to `floor(I * shared_prefix_ratio)` shared-prefix tokens. The resolved independently generated suffix length MUST be `I` minus that entry's resolved shared-prefix length. A zero shared prefix and a zero independently generated suffix MUST both remain valid.

The Bench seed and resolved per-entry shared-prefix schedule MUST determine one canonical shared token stream long enough for the maximum resolved shared-prefix length in the frozen population. Each materialized final prompt MUST begin with the prefix of that canonical stream whose length is resolved for that entry. Content after that prefix MUST be generated independently for the entry. With a proportional declaration and variable input lengths, the resulting shared prefixes MUST therefore be nested prefixes of the same stream rather than unrelated per-length prefixes.

For a fixed selected input length, a token declaration and a ratio declaration that resolve to the same shared-prefix token count MUST produce the same materialized population under the same effective prompt kind, template inputs, seed, and population length. Increasing the required population length MUST preserve the first N selected input targets, resolved shared-prefix lengths, and materialized prompts.

A `flat` source with a resolved shared-prefix length of zero MUST generate independent prompts from the first tokenizer-controlled payload token. A `rendered_chat` source MUST include its frozen template framing in the final common-prefix calculation. If the declared prefix geometry is incompatible with invariant template framing, or the final rendered prompts cannot satisfy both their exact input targets and resolved common-prefix lengths, population preparation MUST fail rather than weaken the declared geometry.

Omission of `prefix_sharing` MUST declare no controlled final-prompt prefix geometry. Materialized prompts MAY still share tokenizer special tokens or invariant rendered-template framing, and evidence MUST NOT describe those incidental tokens as a declared zero-cache-hit outcome.

A `server_chat` random source MAY instead declare one `shared_system_content` table containing exactly one positive integer `tokens` or one finite `ratio` strictly between zero and one. It MUST generate a canonical shared system-message content stream and an independently generated user message. For an entry with selected input target `I`, the token form MUST resolve to its declared fixed pre-template system-content length and the ratio form MUST resolve to `floor(I * ratio)`. Definition resolution MUST reject any declaration for which the resolved system-content length is zero or is not strictly less than `I` for any possible selected input target; the unadjusted user-content length is `I` minus that resolved system-content length. This table describes source message content before server rendering; it MUST NOT be presented as an exact final-prompt prefix, combined with `prefix_sharing`, or used by the `primed` cache-start policy in [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state).

Neither a declared shared-prefix length nor its ratio to a selected or observed input length is a requested cache-hit percentage. InferLab MUST preserve it as workload geometry and MUST use backend cache-read accounting governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state) for observed reuse.

**Rationale:** Fixed tokens model a stable system or repository context across variable request sizes, while a ratio models proportional reuse and naturally produces nested prefixes for distributed ISL. Both declaration forms lower to one per-entry token schedule and one population authority. Inclusive endpoints represent independent flat prompts and full-prompt reuse without claiming that a backend must realize the same cache-read ratio.

*Since: v0.24.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE] Serving Bench Prefix-Cache State (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state"></a>

A serving-Bench definition MAY declare one `cache` table whose `start` is `uncontrolled`, `cold`, or `primed`. Omission MUST resolve to `uncontrolled`. The former `reset_prefix_cache` field MUST be rejected rather than retained as a second cache-state authority.

For `uncontrolled`, InferLab MUST NOT reset or condition the prefix cache for the case. The record MUST NOT claim a known profiling cache state.

For `cold`, the resolved target server MUST provide its server-specific prefix-cache reset capability. Any declared native runtime warmup MUST complete before InferLab invokes that reset. Profiling MUST begin after the successful reset without an intervening conditioning request.

For `primed`, the request source MUST use `flat` or `rendered_chat`, MUST declare `prefix_sharing`, and MUST resolve at least one positive shared-prefix length. The resolved target server MUST provide its server-specific prefix-cache reset capability. Any declared native runtime warmup MUST complete before reset. After a successful reset and before profiling, InferLab MUST complete recorded conditioning whose transport prompt is exactly the canonical shared token stream through the maximum resolved shared-prefix length. On a direct Engine endpoint, InferLab MUST issue one conditioning request per attention data-parallel rank of the public serving role, pinning each request to its rank through the framework's rank-routing request header. On a Gateway-fronted endpoint, conditioning coverage is defined over the cache-owning targets: every model-serving prefill replica and every attention data-parallel rank of that replica. When the serving shape resolves to exactly one such target, ordinary frontend routing cannot miss it, and InferLab MUST issue one conditioning request through the ordinary serving flow without rank pinning, exactly as on a direct Engine endpoint with one rank; a declared fan-out capability is not required for that shape. When more than one cache-owning target exists, InferLab MUST invoke the frontend's conditioning fan-out capability, which MUST route one conditioning request through the ordinary serving flow for every model-serving prefill replica and every attention data-parallel rank of that replica, pinning each request to its rank; decode-side cache state produced by that flow is incidental and MUST be preserved as evidence rather than claimed as coverage. That prompt MUST contain no profiling entry unique suffix and MUST be locally verified to tokenize to exactly those canonical prefix tokens. Conditioning MUST use the same served model, derived completions route, and complete effective `request_body` fragment as profiling, request exactly one output token, and ignore the generated response content. Inability to construct or verify that conditioning prompt MUST fail preparation. Conditioning MUST NOT consume a profiling population entry. A Bench whose cache start is `primed` or whose request source declares prefix sharing MUST be rejected at planning when the resolved server endpoint does not expose backend cache-read usage: the measurement's cache-reuse evidence would otherwise be unobservable, and a completed run MUST NOT fail at normalization for a configuration that was knowable before launch. A `primed` start MUST be rejected before preparation when the public workload endpoint belongs to a Gateway whose serving shape resolves to more than one cache-owning target and whose selected backend does not declare the conditioning fan-out capability: ordinary frontend routing cannot address an individual replica or data-parallel rank, so conditioning could not cover every cache-owning rank.

When a case has a positive AIPerf-native warmup, InferLab MUST hold profiling before its first credit, wait for warmup to drain successfully, then perform the selected reset and conditioning actions before releasing profiling. A case without native warmup MUST complete the selected reset and conditioning actions before its first profiling request. InferLab MUST NOT insert another prefix-cache reset between successful conditioning and profiling.

Warmup and conditioning requests MUST be excluded from normalized profiling counts, SLO evaluation, transport metrics, prompt-token distributions, cache-read metrics, and server-metric deltas. A profiling capture window MUST open after successful reset and conditioning and before profiling is released, so native warmup, reset, and conditioning activity stays outside it. Observing first-execution behavior therefore uses an ordinary case whose resolved warmup request count is zero, not a capture policy over warmup.

A missing required reset capability, failed reset, failed or incomplete conditioning request, lost profiling barrier, or interruption before profiling release MUST fail the case. InferLab MUST NOT intentionally release profiling before preparation succeeds. Any profiling request that escapes the barrier MUST be retained as invalid partial evidence and MUST NOT contribute to successful profiling counts or metrics. Evidence MUST preserve every completed or partial preparation action under [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-PROMPT-CACHE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-prompt-cache-evidence).

The one case budget governed by [RFC-0009:C-MEASUREMENT-CASE-BUDGETS](../rfc/RFC-0009.md#rfc-0009c-measurement-case-budgets) MUST cover native warmup, prefix-cache reset, conditioning, profiling, and result handling. Cleanup MUST retain its separate grace.

A successful profiling request in a case with `prefix_sharing`, `shared_system_content`, or `cache.start = "primed"` MUST provide backend-reported prompt-cache-read tokens as well as backend-reported prompt tokens. An integration endpoint MAY declare that its backend protocol omits cache-read detail exactly when the reported value is zero; only for such an endpoint, that omission MUST be interpreted as the backend-defined representation of integer zero. Without that explicit endpoint capability, missing cache-read usage for any completed profiling request MUST fail successful-result normalization for that case.

For those observed requests, InferLab MUST expose `prompt_cache_read_tokens` and `uncached_prompt_tokens` distribution families, where each request's uncached value equals its backend-reported prompt tokens minus its backend-reported prompt-cache-read tokens. A negative derived value MUST fail normalization. The distribution prefixes and percentile semantics MUST follow [RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-measurements).

The existing `prompt_cache_read_ratio` MUST remain the profiling window total of backend-reported prompt-cache-read tokens divided by the total of backend-reported prompt tokens. It is an observed token-volume-weighted result. When this clause requires per-request cache-read usage, that one recorded integer population MUST be the normalized ratio authority; any AIPerf aggregate remains native corroborating evidence and MUST NOT replace those request observations. A Bench definition MUST NOT declare a target cache-hit or cache-read percentage.

Server-metric collection MAY accompany native warmup and cache preparation. Its normalized deltas and exported profiling window MUST exclude warmup, reset, and conditioning activity.

**Rationale:** Runtime warmup, cache reset, cache conditioning, prefix geometry, and observed cache reads answer different experiment questions. A closed start-state policy makes their order explicit while preserving AIPerf as the profiling engine and treating backend cache behavior as an outcome rather than a promise.

*Since: v0.24.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENT-AUTHORING-DISCOVERY] Measurement Authoring Discovery (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-measurement-authoring-discovery"></a>

The version-matched InferLab CLI long-help surface MUST make the ordinary measurement-authoring path discoverable without requiring an installed agent skill, website, or source checkout. Across `workspace show`, `recipe run`, and `bench` long help, it MUST include accepted TOML examples for a built-in OpenAI smoke using its defaults, a fixed synthetic serving Bench that omits the default definition and prompt kinds, and an inclusive-uniform synthetic Bench whose range tables omit `kind`.

Every published configuration or invocation example in that help MUST be accepted by the same InferLab release and MUST name only supported override paths. The `workspace show --json` help MUST identify that output as the canonical merged workspace representation in which authoring defaults are explicit.

Bundled authoring references and website documentation MAY provide advanced prompt, dataset, session, cache, metrics, SLO, and profiling guidance, but they MUST supplement rather than replace the ordinary CLI-local examples.

**Rationale:** Operators need a short, version-aligned path from an empty definition to a valid ordinary measurement. Keeping those examples beside the parser and canonical workspace projection prevents an agent-only guide or a stale website from becoming the practical schema authority.

*Since: v0.25.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-AGENTIC-TRACE-REPLAY] Serving Bench Agentic Trace Replay (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-agentic-trace-replay"></a>

A static `serving` Bench definition MAY declare `agentic_source` instead of `request_source` or `session_source`. An agentic source represents a release-qualified population of recorded root and subagent session trees whose request geometry, parent-child dependencies, and timing are replayed for serving performance measurement. It MUST NOT be accepted by `adaptive-serving` and MUST NOT expose AIPerf scenario, dataset-loader, timing-mode, cache-bust, plugin, DAG, or arbitrary workflow configuration names.

An `agentic_source` MUST declare a release-qualified `dataset` and `profile`. The selected catalog entry MUST bind the public names to an immutable upstream dataset snapshot, expected content digest, source format, materialization semantics, and the upstream benchmark-script revision that the profile reproduces. A profile MUST bind one closed replay policy including its admissible context-length population, trajectory-start range, global-idle treatment, warmup policy, cache-bust policy, request construction, failure thresholds, minimum and default profiling duration, and required native artifacts. One InferLab release MUST NOT resolve the same catalog or profile name to different source bytes or replay semantics.

A definition MUST declare exactly one of `request_source`, `session_source`, and `agentic_source`. An agentic-backed definition MUST declare a non-empty list of positive `concurrency` values and MAY declare positive `duration_seconds`; omission of duration MUST resolve to the selected profile default, while an explicit value below the profile minimum MUST be rejected. It MAY use the ordinary Bench seed, timeout, server-metric selection, and served-model resolution. It MUST reject request rates, request counts, prompts-per-concurrency, sessions-per-concurrency, ordinary warmup counts, burstiness, prompt declarations, prefix-sharing and cache-start declarations, and open request-body fragments because the release-qualified profile owns those meanings. Invocation overrides MUST NOT change the selected source boundary, dataset, or profile.

The Bench seed MUST deterministically govern trace ordering, trajectory-boundary sampling, and every other replay choice assigned to randomness by the profile. Concurrency MUST mean the maximum number of admitted root session trees. A root tree occupies one lane from admission until its root and every spawned descendant have reached a native terminal state; parent suspension, recorded think time, and child execution do not release that lane. Descendant requests MAY therefore make instantaneous transport-request concurrency greater than the declared root-tree concurrency. When a tree drains during profiling, the native replay scheduler MAY admit the next trace selected by its release-pinned sequential sampling policy.

The immutable upstream trace snapshot MUST remain the authority for source topology, source coordinates, source token and cache-block geometry, and recorded timestamps. During client startup, the release-pinned AIPerf loader MUST acquire or reuse that qualified snapshot, validate and materialize it through its native dataset path, and classify invalid or unsupported traces before transport begins. Acquisition, loader, or materialization failure MUST fail the case without a transport request. InferLab MUST retain the qualified source identity, expected and observed source digest, resolved native configuration, and produced native run artifacts; it MUST NOT require AIPerf to publish an `inputs.json` or a separate materialized graph that the qualified Weka path does not produce, and MUST NOT reconstruct a second authoritative graph.

The release-pinned AIPerf AgentX replay capability MUST own runtime session-tree scheduling. For every admitted trace it MUST reproduce the source parent and subagent topology, admit descendants at their recorded spawn boundaries, suspend a parent at a blocking join, resume it only after the required descendants terminate, preserve per-stream request order, and keep one root lane until the whole tree drains. InferLab MUST NOT translate that topology into its own general DAG, operation graph, or workflow runtime.

The profile MUST use the trace materializer's response-inclusive delta context. Each request history MUST therefore be reconstructed from the source-derived synthetic turn content and response geometry that establish the recorded prefix and cache relationships. A measured live server response MUST remain transport evidence and MUST NOT choose, rewrite, or semantically feed a later source turn. The Bench measures replay serving behavior; it does not claim successful execution of the source agent task or evaluate response quality.

Profiling MUST preserve each stream's recorded request timing relative to its sampled trajectory boundary and preserve recorded inter-turn spacing and dependency order. The release-qualified profile MAY cap a period in which the complete replay would otherwise be globally idle, but it MUST shift all pending timers together and MUST NOT apply an unrecorded per-trace think-time cap, reorder timers, or replace the trace timeline with an InferLab delay distribution. Records MUST preserve the source-timing and global-idle policies plus native source coordinates and observed request timestamps; they MUST NOT claim that AIPerf 0.12 reports each internal timer shift or sampled trajectory boundary when it does not.

Before profiling, AIPerf MUST synthesize one snapshot warmup from the same trajectory population and boundary choices. Every stream active before the boundary MUST replay its last eligible pre-boundary request with its reconstructed prefix; streams that begin at or after the boundary need no snapshot request. Any snapshot warmup failure MUST abort the case before profiling. When the profile declares additional cache-pressure warmup, the same live trajectories MUST continue for the profile duration without recorded idle waits and with the profile's bounded warmup output, drain under the profile grace policy, and then resume profiling from the resulting state with residual next-request delay preserved. Warmup traffic and warmup failures MUST remain separate from profiling metrics. Evidence MUST be limited to the effective policy, emitted warmup records, native phase outcomes, and other fields actually exported by the release-pinned AIPerf artifacts; it MUST NOT fabricate internal handoff state.

Profiling MUST be duration-driven. At the duration boundary, native scheduling MUST stop admitting new work and finalize or classify already admitted trees according to the release-pinned replay contract and ordinary case deadline. A tree or branch classified by AIPerf as truncated solely because the requested profiling window ended is an observable duration outcome and MUST NOT be silently counted as a completed tree or converted into an unrelated transport failure. Cancellation, deadline expiry, missing terminal evidence, or scheduler failure remains a case failure.

The profile MUST use streaming chat-completions requests, server-owned chat rendering, and source-defined output limits, and MUST retain its native cache-bust and scenario-invariant policy. A case succeeds only when AIPerf exits successfully, its native scenario outcome reports a valid submission, the required aggregate artifact including native branch statistics and, at the `diagnostic` artifact level governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-ARTIFACT-LEVEL](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-artifact-level), the required raw-request artifact are present, and InferLab can reconcile the exported fields. InferLab MUST preserve AIPerf's profiling failure-rate and context-overflow decisions and counts and MUST NOT recompute a second acceptance threshold. An early native failure-threshold abort, an invalid scenario outcome, or a required-artifact or reconciliation failure MUST fail the case.

Normalized latency, token, transport-request throughput, and optional server metrics MUST retain the meanings of the measured native transport requests. They MUST NOT be relabeled as root-session, agent, or task-completion metrics. Agentic summaries MUST separately preserve the branch, join, warmup, ordinary-failure, context-overflow, and duration outcomes that the native artifacts actually report. Request-level SLO and adaptive-rate search semantics do not apply to `agentic_source` in this RFC version.

A dry-run MUST resolve the public source and profile, catalog identity, cache path and state, effective replay policy, concurrency cases, seed, duration, endpoint, and planned native invocation without downloading missing data or claiming materialized topology, warmup, runtime, or outcome facts that were not observed.

**Rationale:** SemiAnalysis AgentX is a concrete duration-driven serving workload whose root and subagent trees, timing, and synthetic cache geometry already have a release-pinned native scheduler in AIPerf. A closed `agentic_source` keeps that operator workflow distinct from finite live-response linear sessions while avoiding an InferLab-owned DAG language, avoiding direct dependence on a serving engine's benchmark client, and staying within AIPerf 0.12's qualified public artifact boundary.

*Since: v0.26.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENT-DATA-ASSETS] Measurement Data Asset Preparation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-measurement-data-assets"></a>

A measurement data asset is non-synthetic source content selected by an effective Eval task or Bench source and needed to construct measurement inputs. The effective task, Bench definition, or release catalog that selected the content MUST remain the sole authority for dataset choice, subset, split, filtering, request construction, and scoring semantics. Preparation MUST NOT introduce a second dataset selector or let a common asset declaration override that authority.

InferLab MUST distinguish three identities. A preparation-attempt identity identifies one effective source selection before external effects begin. An acquired-source identity identifies the resolved content closure made locally available by that attempt. A consumer-materialization identity identifies the lm-eval task data, AIPerf-native representation, or InferLab-frozen population later derived by the owning measurement execution. A revision, content digest, framework fingerprint, derived-cache key, and frozen-population digest MUST NOT be presented as interchangeable identities.

One preparation owner MUST use one preparation attempt for all consumers whose pre-effect selection keys are equal. That key MUST be established before the first source-resolution or acquisition external effect and MUST include the selection authority, acquisition provider and release-pinned acquisition-runtime identity, locator, requested revision or alias, subset, split, filter, data-file selection, local path, and release-catalog identity whenever the field is already selected by effective configuration or catalog data without that effect. Fields discoverable only by the owning resolver after the attempt begins MUST be preserved in effective-selection and acquired-source evidence and MUST NOT retroactively change the attempt identity. Unequal pre-effect selection keys MUST remain separate attempts even if they later resolve to the same effective selection, bytes, or physical cache.

Source preparation is a separately owned, intentionally unbounded, operator-interruptible operation under RFC-0009:C-OPERATION-BUDGETS. It begins immediately before the first source-resolution or acquisition external effect and terminates when every planned attempt is source-ready, one attempt fails, or the operator interrupts it. An external attempt MAY retain a source- or tool-owned responsiveness cap, but source preparation MUST NOT gain an arbitrary overall timeout.

Before a recipe launches any serving process, InferLab MUST prepare every source selected by its workload suite, including a source for a measurement that a later Eval gate may skip. A manual Bench targeting an existing server MUST perform the same source preparation before its first transport request. Recipe preparation failure MUST fail the recipe before serving launch. Manual-Bench preparation failure MUST fail the Bench without stopping, restarting, or otherwise changing its target server.

For a release-qualified source, source-ready means that all declared remote and local source bytes are available, the complete catalog-owned content closure is immutably identified and bound, and every required integrity check succeeded. For a task-owned or operator-owned source, preparation MUST establish that same closed result when the owning interface supports it. When that interface cannot expose or bind a complete closure, preparation MAY instead declare the source opaque and ready only for a non-reproducible execution. An opaque source MAY perform further file access or remote acquisition during consumer materialization; evidence MUST state that preparation did not establish complete local availability. Source preparation MUST NOT send an inference request.

Consumer materialization MUST follow its existing measurement owner rather than being assigned uniformly to a case. Eval task and tokenizer materialization remain Eval-case actions under RFC-0009:C-MEASUREMENT-CASE-BUDGETS. Independent-request and linear-session frozen populations remain owned once by the Bench child before its first case, and every case MUST reference the shared population under RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES or RFC-0004:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSIONS. That Bench-wide materialization is a separate intentionally unbounded, operator-interruptible operation beginning immediately before its first materialization effect and terminating when the population is ready, materialization fails, or the operator interrupts it; it MUST NOT consume an arbitrary case's timeout. AgentX native validation and materialization remain client-startup actions of each AIPerf case and consume that case budget under RFC-0004:C-BENCH-AGENTIC-TRACE-REPLAY and RFC-0009:C-MEASUREMENT-CASE-BUDGETS.

A materialization failure MUST retain the classification of its owner. Eval or AgentX case-owned failure is a case failure. An independent-request or linear-session shared-population failure is a pre-case Bench-child failure. A prelaunch source-preparation failure MUST NOT be relabeled as either materialization failure.

Preparation MUST delegate source-specific resolution and acquisition semantics to the authority selected by the effective source. Hugging Face-backed content MUST use the applicable release-pinned Hugging Face acquisition runtime. A release catalog entry with an explicit URL and digest MUST continue to use the InferLab content-addressed acquisition governed by RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES. InferLab MUST NOT parse private Hugging Face, lm-eval, or AIPerf cache layouts or make one tool consume another tool's derived cache representation.

A source selected by an InferLab release-qualified catalog MUST resolve to the catalog's immutable identity, close every remote content dependency declared by that catalog, and satisfy every expected digest before preparation succeeds. Failure to acquire, bind, or verify that complete closure MUST fail preparation. It MUST NOT fall back to a mutable alias or opaque execution.

For task-owned or operator-owned remote content, preparation MUST resolve a mutable selector to an immutable identity when the owning interface provides one and MUST bind the consumer to that identity when supported. The execution MAY be classified as reproducible only when the complete remote content closure actually consumed is immutably identified and bound. An immutable repository revision is insufficient when a loader obtains additional unbound remote content. When complete immutable binding is unavailable, execution MAY proceed only through the opaque non-reproducible path with a specific reason.

When the owning resolver can enumerate and bind the complete regular-file closure of task-owned or operator-owned local content, InferLab MUST snapshot those files into an immutable prepared location before serving launch or the first manual-Bench request and MUST make the consumer read that snapshot. The acquired-source identity MUST preserve an ordered list of normalized source-root-relative paths and the SHA-256 digest of each file; InferLab MUST NOT invent an aggregate directory digest with semantics the owning resolver did not provide. When the resolver cannot enumerate or bind the complete closure, the owning consumer MAY read the original local source only through the opaque non-reproducible path; evidence MUST preserve the unresolved original path and missing-closure reason and MUST NOT claim an immutable prepared snapshot. Local paths remain subject to the unredacted local-record policy of RFC-0005:C-EVIDENCE.

Eval and Bench preparation in one execution MUST receive identical explicit `HF_HOME`, `HF_HUB_CACHE`, `HF_DATASETS_CACHE`, and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` bindings when those values are operator-selected. Unset-path derivation MUST be delegated to each applicable release-pinned Hugging Face runtime rather than reimplemented by InferLab. Evidence MUST preserve every effective source and dataset cache store reported by the acquisition runtime for each attempt. A verified immutable byte-cache hit MUST avoid downloading those source bytes, but metadata access MAY still occur and MUST remain distinguishable from byte acquisition.

Hugging Face source caches, Hugging Face dataset caches, lm-eval and AIPerf derived caches, and InferLab's digest-addressed release cache MUST remain independently owned physical stores. Per-store outcomes MUST distinguish full hit, miss, partial reuse, and unavailable observation, and MUST distinguish remote metadata access from source-byte download or reuse. Successfully acquired cache content is recoverable machine-local state and MUST NOT be rolled back solely because a later preparation, serving, Eval, or Bench step fails.

Dry-run MUST inspect the effective selection, already-local source state, and existing materializations without external access, download, cache mutation, or persisted materialization. It MAY compute deterministic materialization facts purely from locally available inputs when doing so has no external or persisted side effect, preserving the existing dry-run obligations of RFC-0004:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCES. It MUST otherwise report planned attempts and unavailable identities or outcomes rather than claim successful resolution, acquisition, verification, reproducibility, or materialization.

**Rationale:** Eval and Bench retain different source and materialization semantics, but both need acquisition failure and reproducibility evidence settled before recipe-owned serving resources are occupied. One source-preparation boundary supplies that invariant without replacing the distinct Eval-case, Bench-wide population, and AgentX-case materialization owners.

*Since: v0.27.0*

### [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-ARTIFACT-LEVEL] Serving Bench Artifact Level (Normative) <a id="rfc-0004c-bench-artifact-level"></a>

A serving-Bench definition MAY declare `artifact_level` as `performance` or `diagnostic`. Omission MUST resolve to `diagnostic`. The effective artifact level MUST be preserved in canonical merged workspace output, dry-run, execution, and record evidence whether it was declared or defaulted.

At the `diagnostic` level, InferLab MUST request the measurement runtime's full per-request raw request/response export for the case. At the `performance` level, InferLab MUST NOT request that raw export and MUST still obtain the runtime's normalized per-request records and summary export. The artifact level MUST NOT alter the effective request population, load shape, warmup policy, request-body fragment, endpoint selection, server-metric collection, or normalized metric semantics of the case.

Warmup success and failure validation and population-identity reconciliation MUST be evaluated from the normalized per-request records, which carry the native benchmark-phase marker for the warmup and profiling phases, and MUST NOT require the raw request/response export under either artifact level.

A `performance` case with a `session_source` or `agentic_source` remains a valid case. Evidence dimensions that depend on the raw request/response export degrade under [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSION-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-linear-session-evidence) and [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-AGENTIC-TRACE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-agentic-trace-evidence); the degradation MUST be recorded and MUST NOT fail the case by itself.

**Rationale:** Full raw request/response retention is a diagnostic artifact with material host and export cost on long-output workloads, while normalized records already carry the phase and identity markers that case validation needs. Making raw capture an explicit level keeps ordinary performance runs lean without weakening diagnostic capability, and degradation recording keeps session and agentic evidence honest when the raw artifact is absent.

*Since: v0.29.0*

### v0.32.0 (2026-08-23)

### v0.31.0 (2026-08-23)

Add the replay serving-Bench request source

#### Added

- a replay request source replays an operator-curated population file as the sole content-addressed population authority, with optional expected digest, uniform warmup/profiling partitioning, prefix-sharing geometry, and cache-state conditioning per ADR-0040

### v0.30.2 (2026-08-22)

Exempt single-target Gateway shapes from the primed fan-out capability

#### Fixed

- a Gateway-fronted primed start whose serving shape resolves to exactly one cache-owning target (one prefill replica with attention DP size one) no longer requires a declared conditioning fan-out capability; the multi-target rejection is unchanged

### v0.30.1 (2026-08-21)

Reject profiler declarations when profiling resolves off

#### Changed

- for engine-trace targets the window-closing request dispatches into the one global finalization budget; delivery failure is the window-closing control failure adjudicated by coverage, and a slow or absent response is neutral flush-pending evidence

#### Fixed

- a profiler.mechanism or profiler escape declaration whose server resolves profiling off must fail resolution with a typed enable-profiling remediation instead of silently dropping the declaration
- drop the falsified rule that a successful engine-trace window-closing response equals artifact flush completion; coverage verification is the sole completion verdict

### v0.30.0 (2026-08-21)

Generalize workload profiling to pluggable capture mechanisms

- Gateway-fronted primed starts condition every prefill replica and data-parallel rank through a declared frontend fan-out capability; Gateways without the capability reject primed starts
- cache-evidence-requiring Benches (primed or prefix-sharing sources) are rejected at planning when the endpoint exposes no backend cache-read usage

#### Changed

- engine-trace coverage verification is a dedicated-directory storage delta of at least one new artifact per rank, and the trace directory is keyed by server definition and replica under record-owned runtime storage

#### Fixed

- primed cache start issues one pinned conditioning request per attention data-parallel rank and rejects primed starts whose Gateway fronted roles use attention data parallelism
- engine-trace coverage counts one new artifact per device of the replica's whole-replica device count, since engine profilers write per worker process rather than per control-plane entry rank
